stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding the management of acute leukemias:

options.html: The treatment for acute myeloid leukemia (AML) involves the use of high dose steroids, vincristine, asparaginase, anthracyclines.
The treatment of acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) treatment does not involve central nervous system prophylaxis (CNS).

Stem cell transplantation is not a useful treatment modality in patients with acute myeloid leukemia.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Patients with ALL are treated with steroids, vincristine, asparaginase and anthracyclines. ALL treatment does involve CNS prophylaxis. Stem cell transplantation can be used in AML.

lectureMeta: The knowledge checks inside the week's Elentra asynchronous learning modules, transcribed into the Meds 2025 question bank.
stem: Patients presenting with acute myeloid leukemia (AML) may present with many signs, symptoms and laboratory abnormalities. Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding the presentation of AML?

options.html: Anemia is a common finding in patients with newly diagnosed AML
Leukocytosis and blastocytosis are commonly seen at the time of diagnosis.
Thrombocytopenia is a common finding in AML.
Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) should be ruled out in all patients presenting with AML.
Leukemia cutis is never seen in patients at time of diagnosis of AML.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Patients can present with anemia, leukocytosis, blastocytosis and thrombocytopenia at the time of diagnosis. Leukemia cutis can be seen at the time of diagnosis and in many patients is a presenting feature. DIC is a common and serious complication of AML and should be ruled out in all patients with AML.

lectureMeta: The knowledge checks inside the week's Elentra asynchronous learning modules, transcribed into the Meds 2025 question bank.
stem: Which of the following statements is FALSE regarding the management of acute myeloid leukemias:

options.html: Patients with good risk cytogenetic are generally treated with chemotherapy alone.
Patients with good risk cytogenetics require a stem cell transplantation.
Some patients with acute promyelocytic leukemia can be treated with arsenic trioxide and all-trans-retinoic-acid (ATRA) alone.
Stem cell transplantation should be recommended for patients with poor risk cytogenetics.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Patients with good risk cytogenetics and no evidence of c-kit mutations are generally treated with chemotherapy and only require a transplant if relapse occurs. Some patients with acute promyelocytic leukemia can be treated with arsenic/ATRA alone particularly those that are non-high risk. Patients with poor-risk cytogenetics should be offered a transplant as it provides the best chance of long-term disease control.

stem: Which one of the following scenarios would require the largest sample size to demonstrate superiority in a clinical trial comparing 2 treatments A and B, where PA is the proportion of events expected with treatment A and PB is the proportion of events expected with treatment B?

options.html: Power 80%, a 0.05, PA-PB difference very large

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Of the scenarios listed above, scenario D (Power 90%, a 0.05, PA-PB difference small) will require the largest sample size to show superiority of one treatment over another. Large study numbers are required if we want high power to detect small differences between treatment groups.

stem: Which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.html: A per-protocol or ‘as-treated’ analysis includes an analysis of all patients in the trial
An intention to treat analysis includes an analysis of all eligible patients, regardless of their compliance with the therapy
A per-protocol analysis is always the more conservative form of analysis in a clinical trial
Compared to a per-protocol analysis, an intention to treat analysis always yields a higher effect estimate in a clinical trial
A per-protocol analysis is the preferred form of analysis in most trials

answer:
The correct answer is B.

An intention to treat analysis includes an analysis of all eligible patients, regardless of their compliance with the therapy and follow-up whereas a per-protocol or ‘as-treated’ analysis includes all patients who completed the full course of assigned treatment. An intention to treat analysis is the preferred form of analysis in most trials as it preserves the underlying randomization process. It is usually the conservative form of analysis in the common superiority trial design setting. A per-protocol analysis will usually yield a higher effect estimate of the treatment effect in this setting.

lectureMeta: The knowledge checks inside the week's Elentra asynchronous learning modules, transcribed into the Meds 2025 question bank.
stem: Which of the following about subgroup analyses is TRUE?

options.html: All possible subgroup analyses must be considered and performed in a clinical trial to examine if treatment differences appear consistent across all types of patients or vary according to subgroups
Subgroup analyses are subject to concerns of multiple testing where there is a risk of a false positive result purely by chance alone, if enough statistical tests are performed
Subgroup analyses generally have higher power to detect a therapeutic effect than the primary endpoint
The results of the subgroup analyses are as definitive as the primary analysis

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Subgroup analyses are subject to concerns of multiple testing where there is a risk of a false positive result purely by chance alone, if enough statistical tests are performed. As a result, it is important that only a limited number of pre-specified subgroup analyses be performed with cautious interpretation of findings.

stem: Which of the following statements regarding radiation is false?

options.html: Radiation works by damaging the DNA of cancer cells inhibiting their ability to reproduce
Radiation is therapeutically effective because it is only lethal to cancer cells; normal tissues are able to repair 100% of their DNA damage
DNA damage caused by radiation in cancer cells can cause cell transformation, mutation, and/or trigger apoptosis/cellular death
Radiation creates charged particles in tissue that damage cellular DNA two ways: directly by causing a strand break or indirectly by interacting with water to create free-radicals that damage the DNA

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Statement B is false as radiation can cause DNA damage to normal tissues also, however normal tissues tend to have better and more efficient repair mechanisms than cancer cells, where these mechanisms are often more deranged. We exploit this differential by giving radiation slowly enough to allow time for more of the normal cells to recover, but certainly the repair is not 100%, and is mutative or lethal to some of the normal tissue. At an organ level this is what creates the acute and late/chronic toxicity of treatment.

lectureMeta: The knowledge checks inside the week's Elentra asynchronous learning modules, transcribed into the Meds 2025 question bank.
stem: Cancer cells are susceptible to DNA damage when they are in an active mitotic state. Fractionationating a total radiation treatment dose into multiple daily smaller doses of radiation increases tumour kill ability by allowing cancer cells to cycle and assort themselves into a more radiosenstive phase of the cell cycle. This is best described by which of the 4 R’s of Radiobiology:
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Redistribution (also known as re-assortment, allows time between radiation fractions for cancer cells to distribute themselves into a more radiosensitive phase of the cell cycle. As a reminder, the 4 R’s are: • Repair of sublethal damage to cells between fractions caused by radiation • Repopulation or regrowth of cells between fractions • Redistribution of cells into radiosensitive phases of cell cycle • Reoxygenation of hypoxic cells to make them more sensitive to radiation Fractionation of radiation spares normal tissue through repair and repopulation while increasing damage to tumor cells through redistribution and reoxygenation

stem: Radiation can play multiple roles in a patients care. For a patient presenting to ER with a recurrent metastatic multifocal tumour pressing on a patient’s spinal cord causing leg weakness, (no surgery possible) a moderate dose of radiation can be given to alleviate pain and reduce the risk of permanent neurological compromise. answer:
The correct answer is C.

Radiation is routinely used in both curative and palliative management of cancer patients. Spinal cord compression from a malignant tumour is typically an oncologic emergency, and management typically can include surgery followed by radiation, vs radiation alone. Recognizing the clinical need for urgent referral to a spine surgeon and radiation oncologist for opinion on palliative treatment is critical when encountering this situation in clinical practice.

answer:

lectureMeta: The week's Readiness Assessment, as it was sat.
stem: A 12 year old boy has been admitted with meningococcemia. He has extensive bruising over his body and is also bleeding from venipuncture sites. Blood work shows: Hb 75 g/L [Normal 115-160 g/L], WBC 15.9 x 109/L [Normal 4-10 x 109/L], Platelet 45 x 109/L [Normal 150-400 x 109/L], INR 2.7 [Normal 0.9-1.2], PTT 67 [Normal 29-37]. Peripheral blood smear shows RBC fragments. The MOST likely diagnosis is:
answer:
The correct answer is C.

TTP and HUS may lead to fragmentation but does not lead to derangement of PTT or INR. Also, bleeding is uncommon in this situation. Vit K deficiency can lead to prolongation of the PTT and INR in severe deficiency but may not lead to bleeding and does not lead to fragmentation on blood smear. Therefore, DIC is the most appropriate answer which fits the clinical presentation.

stem: Which anticoagulation agent works by means of Factor Xa inhibition only?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Warfarin inhibits the vitamin K-dependent synthesis of biologically active forms of the clotting factors II, VII, IX and X, as well as the regulatory factors protein C, protein S. LMWH exerts its anticoagulation properties via antithrombin III. Hirudin is the most potent natural inhibitor of thrombin.

stem: A 56 year old healthy man awaiting a hernia repair surgery was found to have an INR of 1.8 [0.9-1.1] and aPTT 32 [25-37s] preoperatively. He has no history of bleeding and is not on any medications. His physical examination was unremarkable except for the left inguinal hernia that was found. Kidney and liver functions are normal. Which of the following is the MOST likely explanation for his abnormal coagulation testing now?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Heparin should affect the PTT more so than INR. FXIII deficiency should not affect the INR or PTT. Acquired FX inhibitor will cause prolongation of both INR and PTT. Early forms of Vit K deficiency often leads to prolongation of the INR first due to the shorter halflife of FVII. In prolonged severe Vit K deficiency, both the INR and PTT can be affected.

preamble.html:
The following case scenario and image apply to questions 5 and 6:

An 82 year old healthy man comes in for his yearly physical. On examination, he has mild

axillary lymphadenopathy and slight splenomegaly. Complete blood count [CBC] showed a

WBC of 30x109/L [4-10 x 109/L], platelet count of 140x 109/L [150-400 x 109/L], normal

MCV, and normal hematocrit. His peripheral blood smear is shown.

stem: What is the most likely diagnosis
answer:
The correct answer is C.

stem: A 67 year old male presents in your clinic with fever, fatigue, loss of appetite and severe shoulder and knee pain. He has lost 10% of his body weight over the past two months, and also complains of frequent infections over that time period. His blood work reveals Hb of 95 g/L [normal = 140-180 g/L], a white count of 2.2 x 109/L [5.0-12.0], neutrophil count of 1.2 x 109/L [2.0 - 7.5], and platelet count of 198 (150 - 400 x 109 /L). His blood smear reveals neoplastic plasma cells and stacks of RBCs. You suspect the patient has a plasma cell dyscrasia. What are four features that would help confirm a diagnosis of multiple myeloma.
answer:
The correct answer is A, C, D, F.

Myeloma defining events include "CRAB", SFLC ratio >100 with involved light chain ratio of >100, BM plasma cells >60% and 2 or more MRI myelomatous lesions of 5mm or larger. Therefore, C and F would be correct. A and D would be indicative of presence of a clonal plasma cell disorder. Lymphadenopathy is an uncommon feature in myeloma. Hypercalcemia instead of hypocalcemia occurs in myeloma.

stem: A 55 year old male presented to the emergency room with profuse bleeding from nose and mouth. He appeared very pale with multiple skin bruises and ulcers. answer:
The correct answer is B.

Factor VIII will be decreased in DIC due to consumption but increased in liver disease due to reflex increase as FVIII is produced by the endothelial cells as opposed to liver. Factor V will be decreased in both DIC and Liver disease.

The cell cycle is important to chemotherapy because chemotherapeutic drugs target and disrupt different phases of the cell cycle. Most chemotherapy drugs act on reproducing cells (not those in the G0 phase - the resting phase).

stem: A 78 year old woman has an indolent, low grade lymphoma involving her right cervical chain. It measures <2 cm by clinical measurement. CT of her chest, abdomen and pelvis showed enlarged mediastinal and retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy. She continues to be active, lives alone and has no B symptoms. The correct treatment recommendation at this time would be:
answer:
The correct answer is B.

In asymptomatic indolent B cell lymphoma beyond stage I in a radiation field, treatment is palliative and often reserved until the patient presents with the symptomatic disease as early treatment has not shown any benefits in terms of survival when compared to initiation of therapy when symptomatic. Certainly discussion with the patient when forming a therapeutic plan is pertinent as watchful waiting in an unwilling patient could induce significant anxieties and a poor therapeutic relationship

lectureMeta: The week's Self-Assessment, as it was released.
stem: Which of the following is/are true regarding superior vena cava syndrome:

options.html: This is characteristic of Hodgkin lymphoma.
Can be caused by mediastinal mass
It is characteristic to present with edema of the face and arms

answer:
The correct answer is B, C, E.

Superior vena cava syndrome (SVCS) is a group of symptoms that occur when there is pressure on the superior vena cava, or it is partially blocked and blood can't flow back to the heart normally. This causes more pressure in the veins and face, which leads to a buildup of fluid or swelling. In Hematology, this is often from obstruction from a mass such as mediastinal mass with a positive Pemberton sign on exam and edema to face and arms on inspection

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following clinical markers will NOT significantly differentiate anemia of chronic inflammation from iron deficiency anemia?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Serum iron would be low with anemia of chronic inflammation, as it can’t leave ferritin stores (due to hepcidin interference). Iron in the plasma would be low with iron deficiency for numerous reasons: higher demand, decreased consumption, decreased intestinal absorption and increased loss. During chronic inflammation cytokine levels rise along with Ferritin (as iron cannot leave Ferritin stores). Transferrin – the transport protein for iron is expressed in higher concentrations in Iron deficiency anemia, and in lower concentrations in anemia of chronic inflammation.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following instances is NOT an underlying cause of anemia from iron deficiency?

options.html: Pregnancy leading to an increase in demand of Iron
A genetic mutation that results in reduced intestinal absorption of Iron
A genetic mutation that leads to an absence/reduction of α- or β-globin chains

answer:
The correct answer is C.

A genetic mutation that leads to an absence/reduction of globin chains leads to anemia from Thalassemia. This results in an increased red blood cell count and a normal RDW.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Vitamin B6 deficiency is most commonly associated with which form of anemia?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

In sideroblastic anemia, the body’s ability to synthesize porphyrin is negatively impacted. Vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) is a precursor in porphyrin synthesis. Other causes of sideroblastic anemia include lead poisoning or mutations in the enzymes that synthesize porphyrin (Eg, ALA synthase).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following markers would you use to diagnose β-Thalassemia?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

HbA is normal adult hemoglobin, hemoglobin H is characteristic of α-thalassemia (4 β chains), RBC count is elevated in both α- and β-thalassemia. HbA2 is elevated in β- thalassemia due to a compensatory effect of making more delta-globin chains in place of deficient levels of β-chains, and consists of two α-globin subunits and two δ-globin subunits.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with long term fatigue. Her Hb is 97 g/L [normal 115-160 g/L], and her MCV is 77 fL [normal 80-96 fL]. Past medical history includes rheumatoid arthritis, and additional blood work reveals high ferritin levels and low serum iron levels. Which type of anemia is at the top of your differential diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Anemia of chronic inflammation can be caused by inflammatory conditions such as rheumatoid arthritis, or Crohn’s disease. This is a form of microcytic anemia resulting in higher ferritin levels and lower transferrin levels.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with microcytic anemia. A blood film test is performed, and the following result is obtained. The CBC indicates a normal RDW. What is the patient’s likely diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is E.

When a patient presents with microcytic anemia and target cells on a blood film, it indicates a form of thalassemia, especially when the RDW is normal (uniform size of RBC). Target cells can be observed with iron deficiency anemia, but with IDA the RDW would be elevated. Target cells are red blood cells with a circular dense central region. (Note - further testing would be required to differentiate between β- and α-thalassemia).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are performing your family medicine rotation during clerkship. A patient presents with suspected α-thalassemia. Which ONE test would confirm the diagnosis?

options.html: Presence of basophilic stippling in the blood film
Gene sequencing of the α-globin genes

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Hemoglobin electrophoresis can be used to positively diagnose β-thalassemia but it can miss α-thalassemia. To diagnose α-thalassemia, genetic sequencing is required. (While high RBC count, reticulocyte count, and basophilic stippling is associated with thalassemia, it could not be used to differentiate between β- and α-thalassemia.)

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Key Feature Question: Select Three Answers. A patient presents with a reduced reticulocyte count and a significant reduction in red blood cells, white blood cells and platelets. Which of the following pathologies are most likely?
answer:
The correct answer is A, C, G.

Aplastic Anemia is characterized by decreased production of RBC, WBC, and Platelets. Myelodysplastic syndrome and Myelofibrosis are both bone marrow pathologies that have the potential to lead to pancytopenia (reduction in RBC, WBC, and Platelets). Hemolysis, Anemia of Chronic Inflammation and Blood Loss would present with increased reticulocyte count. Pure Red Cell Aplasia would not affect WBC and platelet levels.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is NOT a sign of pathological hemolysis?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Hemolysis would lead to increased reticulocytosis, as the body is trying to compensate for the lysed RBCs.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient with normocytic anemia also has a low reticulocyte count, and no bone marrow pathology. Which of the following pathologies best explain this?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Aplastic anemia and Myelofibrosis are both bone marrow pathologies. Hemolysis would be characterized by a high reticulocyte count. Anemia from chronic inflammation is marked by decreased production in red blood cells (low reticulocytes) and does not originate from the bone marrow. With time, this would likely lead to microcytic anemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which statement on the topic of reticulocytes is true?

options.html: A reticulocyte is an erythrocyte progenitor
A reticulocyte is an undifferentiated hematopoietic stem cell
Reticulocyte counts are high for aplastic anemia
Reticulocyte counts are higher in times of decreased erythrocyte production

answer:
The correct answer is A.

A reticulocyte is the immediate precursor to red blood cells, and will be elevated during hemolysis. With aplastic anemia, the bone marrow is empty, and reticulocyte counts are low.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents to your clinic complaining of fatigue. He is anemic, with MCV of 85 fL [normal 80-96 fL]. Retic count is very low, and blood film analysis is positive for teardropshaped RBCs. What is the likely diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

In myelophthisis, bone marrow is replaced with other cells. This condition is associated with teardrops in the blood film.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following best explains the pathophysiology for megaloblastic anemia?

options.html: A lack of Vitamin B12 leads to the rapid division of the red blood cell precursor
Cholesterol and phospholipids are deposited into the plasma membrane of the red blood cell
The cell cycle cannot progress from the G2 growth phase into mitosis, so there is cytoplasmic growth without division
Plasma concentration becomes hypotonic, which leads to fluid flowing into the cell leading to an enlarged appearance and dysfunction

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Option C explains the pathophysiology of megaloblastic anemia. Option A is incorrect – Megaloblastic anemia is characterized by halted replication and fewer red blood cells overall. Option B is characteristic of a type of non-megaloblastic anemia, liver disease.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which statement on the topic of macrocytic anemia below is true?

options.html: Vitamin B12 deficiency is associated with non-megaloblastic anemia.
Folate deficiency is associated with elevated methylmalonic acid and homocysteine.
Liver disease results in primarily spherocytes on the blood film.
Nutritional deficiencies associated with macrocytic anemia result in blood cell progenitors arrested in G2 phase.
A patient with hypothyroidism will present with a history of weight loss and elevated heart rate.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Nutritional deficiencies associated with macrocytic anemia are vitamin B12 and folate deficiencies. These result in an arrest in G2 phase, leading to megaloblastic anemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with macrocytic anemia. A blood film is ordered and neutrophils with hyper-segmented neutrophils are observed. The patient rarely drinks alcohol and thorough mental status and neurological examination is unremarkable. This presentation would be most typical of which of the following cause for anemia?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Hypersegmented neutrophils in the blood film could indicate either Vitamin B12 or folate deficiency. A Vitamin B12 deficiency would lead to an excess of methylmalonic acid, leading to neurotoxicity. Since the neurological exam is unremarkable, the more likely diagnosis is folate deficiency. The comment about alcohol in the question stem is a distractor.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: What type of red blood cell would be observed in a blood film of a patient with alcoholrelated anemia?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Alcohol consumption increases lipid concentrations in the blood, which incorporate themselves into red blood cells. With an increased membrane, the red blood cell adjusts its shape into a more energy-efficient one, leading to target cells.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A physician orders a reticulocyte count and then a Coombs test which comes back positive for IgG. Which of the following pathologies is the most likely diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

A positive coombs test (DAT) rules in immune related conditions, and the presence of IgG on the surface of RBCs suggest Warm Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: How does a G6PD deficiency lead to hemolysis?

options.html: The absence of G6PD leads to structural protein defects creating a more spherical cell shape.
The absence of G6PD prevents the formation of certain globin chains
The absence of G6PD leads to the cells clumping together in circulation.
The absence of G6PD leads to the production of free radicals.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

G6PD plays a role in reducing oxidative stress by inactivating free radicals, and without it, oxidative stress would increase leading to hemolysis.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Complete the following sentence: Microangiopathic hemolytic anemia is characterized by the presence of __________ in the blood film.
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Fragmented RBCs (Schistocytes) can be the result of RBCs being forced through smaller veins and fragmenting. This is a type of mechanical damage to RBCs.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which clinical marker would NOT indicate hemolytic anemia?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

The four tests confirming hemolysis are elevated bilirubin (a breakdown product of heme), elevated LDH (an enzyme released into the plasma after hemolysis of RBCs), reduced haptoglobin (haptoglobin sequesters plasma-heme), and increased reticulocyte count (signifying increased blood cell synthesis.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with fatigue and jaundice. Blood work indicates an elevated reticulocyte count. A blood film is obtained, shown below. What is the likely diagnosis based on the blood film?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Observed on the blood panel are clear schistocytes, or red blood cell fragments. This is a type of mechanical damage, which could be caused forcing blood cells through very small blood vessels (micro = small, angio = blood vessels)

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with hemolytic anemia. Which test would not be helpful in determining the underlying cause?
answer:
The correct answer is E.

LDH levels would confirm hemolytic anemia, but would not be useful in differentiating the underlying cause of hemolytic anemia.

stem: Which of the below descriptions of a cell is true?

options.html: Rouleaux: red blood cells when they are clustered together in large groups
Spherocytes: Lost a central pallor, elongated and smaller than usual
Acanthocytes: irregular cytoplasmic projections, lost central pallor

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Rouleaux have RBCs stacked on top of each other like a roll of coins. Spherocytes are spherical and not elongated. Elliptocytes have a central pallor.

stem: Which of the following is not included on a complete blood count?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Monocyte count is included in the white cell differential also referred to as “diff”.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem:
Which of the following conditions can lead to the agglutination of red blood cells?

  1. Cold autoimmune hemolytic anemia
  2. Chronic inflammation
  3. Sickle cell disease variant SS
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Cold AIHA is mediated by IgM binding to RBCs at “cold” temperatures (i.e. below body temperature). IgM can form pentamers and allow RBCs to come together. Hence, it is also called cold agglutinin disease. In Sickle Cell Disease, deoxygenated hemoglobin have a tendency to form long polymers and elongate RBCs. In chronic inflammation, leukocytes often aggregate at the site of inflammation, not red blood cells.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient with a mutation in one copy of their β-globin gene on Chromosome 11 is at risk of developing which condition?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Sickle cell disease and Beta thalassemia are classified as autosomal recessive conditions where two copies must sustain mutations. However Beta Thalassemia minor can develop in patients who are heterozygous for the mutation (they have one mutated copy and one wildtype.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: From gestation to the first year of life a child’s hemoglobin F is replaced with hemoglobin A. Which of the following changes normally occur in the globin chains around birth?

options.html: A decline in the synthesis of the β-globin around birth
A rise in the synthesis of the α-globin around birth
A decline in the synthesis of γ-globin around birth
A decline in the synthesis of δ-globin around birth

answer:
The correct answer is C.

The γ-subunit declines near the time of birth, while the β-subunit rises during the time of birth. The α-subunit rises in gestation and is stable around birth. The α-subunit and the β- subunit form Hemoglobin A (adult hemoglobin which is a tetramer composed of 2 α- and 2 β-globins).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 4-year-old female patient has symptoms of β-thalassemia major. Genetic analysis confirms the diagnosis. Which statement below is true?

options.html: Due to the high severity of symptoms at a young age, the patient likely has mutations in three of the four β-globin genes
In red blood cells, this patient has an excess of Hb S hemoglobin molecules
It is likely that both of this patient’s parents are heterozygous carriers of β- thalassemia
Hemoglobin molecules in this patient likely have two α-subunits and two γ-subunits
This patient likely has a qualitative mutation of the β-globin gene

answer:
The correct answer is C.

β-thalassemia major is mainly a recessive condition in contrast to β-thalassemia minor observed in heterozygotes. Since this patient’s symptoms are severe, this patient likely has two deficient copies of the β-globin gene. This means that the parents must be carriers. Thalassemias are the result of reduced synthesis of the β- or α-globins, and are therefore quantitative mutations.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which statement below on the topic of sickle-cell anemia is false?

options.html: Sickle-cell disease was the first genetic disorder whose molecular basis was known.
Genetic screening for sickle-cell disease is mandatory for newborns in Canada.
Sickle-cell anemia geographically coincides with regions of higher rates of malaria.
Sickle-cell anemia is the result of a mutation causing a Val-->Glu transition of β- globin.
A diagnosis for sickle-cell anemia in adults involves Hb electrophoresis/HPLC.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Sickle-cell anemia is the result of a mutation causing a Glu-->Val transition in the 6th amino acid of the β-globin chain.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following markers would you use to distinguish a folate deficiency from a Vitamin B12 deficiency?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Homocysteine is converted into methionine, and since both Vitamin B12 and Folate play a role in methionine synthesis, a reduction in Methionine or an increase in Homocysteine cannot be used to distinguish the two. Only Vitamin B12 assists in the production of Succinyl CoA from MMA, thus an increase in MMA can indicate a Vitamin B12 deficiency.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem:
Which of the following relationships between globin and oxygen are true?

  1. Fetal hemoglobin has a stronger affinity for oxygen than adult hemoglobin
  2. Myoglobin has a stronger affinity for oxygen than adult and fetal hemoglobin
  3. Carbon monoxide has a stronger affinity for hemoglobin than oxygen.
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Fetal hemoglobin has a stronger affinity for oxygen than adult hemoglobin so it can take oxygen from the mother’s hemoglobin. Myoglobin has a higher affinity for oxygen than adult hemoglobin and fetal hemoglobin, so that the oxygen can be transferred to muscles from circulation.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which pair of lab results indicates a folate deficiency?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Elevated methylmalonic acid is associated with a vitamin B12 deficiency. Folate deficiency would not have elevated methylmalonic acid but would have elevated homocysteine.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: The body has several proteins responsible for iron storage and iron transport. Which definition or function below is true?

options.html: Transferrin is a membrane protein that transfers iron from intestinal cells to blood.
Ferritin is only found within cells.
Hepcidin is an iron-storage complex that can be seen with Perl’s stain.
Divalent metal transporter proteins uptake Fe2+ from the intestines.
Each hemoglobin subunit binds to four iron atoms.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Transferrin transports iron in the blood. Ferritin is an iron storage inside the blood. Hepcidin helps in the transport of iron from intestinal cells to the blood. Finally, each hemoglobin subunit binds to one iron atom, for a total of 4 iron atoms per hemoglobin molecule.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following would you NOT see in a patient with Myelodysplastic Syndrome?

options.html: Immature blood cells in peripheral circulation
Acquired mutations in bone marrow cells

answer:
The correct answer is C.

An MCV below normal would indicate microcytic anemia – Myelodysplastic Syndrome is often characterized by macrocytic anemia, with a reduction in all blood cells (including platelets), immature cells in the bloodstream and can be acquired through genetic mutations in the bone marrow.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following therapies is appropriate for patients with high-risk Myelodysplastic Syndrome, but not appropriate for low-risk Myelodysplastic Syndrome patients?

options.html: Transfusing Hematopoietic growth factors (such as erythropoietin)

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Blood transfusion and transfusing hematopoietic growth factors are options available for both high risk and low risk MDS patients. Hematopoietic stem cell transplant is a therapy only available to high-risk patients with MDS that are relatively healthy.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 76-year-old frail patient presents with fatigue. Blood tests suggest normocytic anemia, and reticulocyte count is low. A bone marrow biopsy is performed, and the bone marrow appears abnormal with dysplasia in at least 2 lineages but no indication of infiltrating tumour cells. Ferritin and serum iron are both high. The patient also has poor prognostic factors as evaluated by the IPSS scoring system (Hemoglobin 82, Platelets 78, complex cytogenetics, 7% blasts in BM). Which option below correctly identifies a diagnosis and a suitable treatment?

options.html: Myelodysplastic syndrome – hematopoietic stem cell transplant
Pure red cell aplasia – aggressive chemotherapy

answer:
The correct answer is A.

An abnormal bone marrow indicates myelodysplasia. The patient has poor prognostic factors (IPSS) in addition to his old age and frailty. He would not qualify hematopoietic stem cell transplant but would qualify for hypomethylating agents.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with suspected myelodysplastic syndrome. Which observation is most likely to rule out a diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Myelodysplastic syndrome is associated with pancytopenia, and accordingly, reduced reticulocytes. Myelodysplastic syndrome can present as normocytic/macrocytic anemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient has the following conditions: macrocytic anemia, hyper-segmented neutrophils, significant weight loss and substantial atrophy of brain tissue. Out of the following causes for his presentation which is the most probable?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Macrocytic anemia, hyper-segmented neutrophils and significant weight loss are all signs of Megaloblastic macrocytic anemia, which primarily has two culprits listed: folate deficiency and vitamin B12 deficiency. Only Vitamin B12 deficiency leads to defect in neurological tissue. Other causes of a megaloblastic macrocytic anemia include myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) or medications such as methotrexate, anti-folate antagonist.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Key feature question: Select two answers. A prescription of erythropoietin would be MOST beneficial for patients with the following conditions:
answer:
The correct answer is C, D.

Erythropoietin (EPO) is a growth factor mainly produced by the kidneys that stimulates red blood cell growth. Patients with acute renal failure may have reduced endogenous erythropoietin (EPO), and patients with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS) could use extra erythropoietin to stimulate erythropoiesis. Note, aplastic anemia involves empty bone marrow and therefore erythropoietin would have minimum effect in red blood cell synthesis (ie erythropoiesis). EPO administration may be considered for the other conditions but is typically not the predominant treatment. Further for EPO to work appropriately, the other building blocks such as iron, vitamin B12 and folate have to be adequately replaced.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following connects the correct main site of absorption for each supplement?

options.html: Iron in the duodenum, folate and B12 in the terminal ileum
Iron and folate in the duodenum, B12 in the terminal ileum
Iron, folate, and B12 in the duodenum
Iron, folate, and B12 in the terminal ileum

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Iron and folate in the duodenum, B12 in the terminal ileum. Recall that iron is absorbed in the duodenum and proximal jejunum. Folate is absorbed in the duodenum. Although vitamin B12 can be absorbed by passive diffusion throughout the gastrointestinal tract, the main site of absorption is bound to intrinsic factor at the terminal ileum.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following would be the MOST likely cause for B12 deficiency anemia?

options.html: Surgical resection of the colon and part of the small intestine attached to the colon

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Surgical resection of the terminal ileum which is the part of the small intestine attached to the colon. Chronic blood loss would lead to iron deficiency anemia. Trauma to the spleen would cause acute blood loss and a normocytic anemia. Hypothyroidism is associated with a macrocytic anemia but not B12 deficiency.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: What are the two premetabolites that will be increased if vitamin B12 is deficient?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Vitamin B12 is involved in only 2 metabolic pathways in the human body. It converts methylmalonic acid to succinyl CoA and homocysteine to methionine. With vitamin B12 deficiency, these premetabolites methylmalonic acid (MMA) and homocysteine build up and are elevated.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 45-year-old man has had progressive weakness and dyspnea with exertion for 3 months. He appears malnourished; the conjunctivae are pale, and there are scattered petechiae. He has been under stress from the pandemic and lost his job 6 months ago. His diet consists of water and occasional scraps he can find. Laboratory studies show: Hemoglobin 98 g/L (N: 135-180); MCV: 109 fL (N: 80-100); leukocyte count: 4.5 E9/L (N: 4-10) with hypersegmented neutrophils; reticulocyte count: 0.5%; platelet count: normal. The MOST likely cause of his condition is deficiency of which of the following?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Folic acid deficiency. Although, it is very likely that he could be deficient in multiple nutrients and minerals, his macrocytic anemia and hyper-segmented neutrophils point to a megaloblastic anemia. Of the choices, only folic acid or vitamin B12 deficiency could do this. However, it is unlikely that he would have developed vitamin B12 deficiency within 6 months as it often takes years.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is a complication of folate deficiency?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Folic acid deficiency can lead to neural tube defects. This occurs in neonates born to a mother with folic acid deficiency.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: With regards to sleep hygiene, which of the following is a good practice?

options.html: Take naps throughout the day to alleviate tiredness and maintain your sleep cycle
Eat a light bedtime snack if you are hungry
Consume fluid before bed to wake up refreshed
Think about going to sleep when you are in bed

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Eating a light bedtime snack if you’re hungry promotes sleep by reducing hypoglycemia. It’s important to keep an anchored wake time and not to take naps if you haven’t gotten enough sleep as this will reduce your sleep deficit, and possibly alter your sleep cycle. Reduce fluid consumption before bed to prevent a full bladder. Don’t try to think about falling asleep as this leads to frustration and conditioned cognitive arousal.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following sleeping disorders is correctly characterized?

options.html: Insomnia: snoring/gasping, daytime sleepiness, unrefreshed sleep
Obstructive sleep apnea: difficulty initiating/maintaining sleep or early morning awakening
Narcolepsy: Recurrent periods of irrepressible need to sleep
REM sleep behavior disorder: urge to move legs, unpleasant sensation in legs relieved by movement

answer:
The correct answer is C.

The description in option A applies to Obstructive sleep apnea, and the description in option B applies to insomnia. Option D refers to restless leg syndrome.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Key feature question: Select four answers. Which of the following conditions would warrant a referral for polysomnography?
answer:
The correct answer is D, F, H, J.

These answers were taken from the notes for a psychiatrist’s approach to fatigue. Normally, you would not order polysomnography testing for a patient with insomnia, however, this can be considered if traditional management of insomnia is unsuccessful.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is not a central tenet when using cognitive behavioural therapy to treat insomnia?

options.html: Recognize the high importance of sleep
Do not catastrophize after a poor night’s sleep
Develop tolerance to the effects of insomnia

answer:
The correct answer is B.

All of these are central tenets for cognitive behavioural therapy for insomnia except B. Instead, patients should try not to overemphasize the importance of a good night’s sleep, or else they may have elevated anxiety about sleep which may exacerbate their insomnia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following complexes is necessary for the pathway that propagates (amplifies) the coagulation cascade?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

The intrinsic Xase complex is necessary for facilitating the intrinsic pathway which is often regarded as amplifying the cascade that is initiated by the extrinsic pathway (mediated by extrinsic Xase.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following pathways INCORRECTLY describe a stage of a platelet feature in the primary hemostasis pathway?

options.html: The contraction phase involves a change in the shape of the platelet from a spherical shape to a disc shape
The adhesion phase is characterized by surface glycoproteins binding to the sub endothelial area of the injured tissue
The secretion phase involves the influx of calcium inside the cell followed by a release of platelet granules
In the aggregation phase, aggregation is mediated by glycoproteins, including GP IIb/IIIa

answer:
The correct answer is A.

The contraction phase involves the platelets changing from a disc-shape to a spherical shape.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following markers is elevated as a result of fibrinolysis?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

D-dimer is the final product of the fibrinolysis pathway. Cross-linked fibrin present in clots is broken down to D-dimer by plasmin. Thrombin is a procoagulant, and anti-thrombin is an anticoagulant (it stops coagulation but does not play a role in fibrinolysis)

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: For which of the following genetic abnormalities would a patient be expected to bleed more readily?

options.html: A mutation in the gene encoding Protein S which reduces Protein S activity
A mutation in the gene encoding antithrombin, which reduces antithrombin activity
A mutation in the gene encoding Factor XIII, which increases Factor XIII activity
A mutation in the gene encoding Factor V, which reduces Factor V activity
A mutation in the gene encoding Factor XII, which reduces Factor XII activity

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Protein S and antithrombin down-regulate clot formation, so reduced activity of these will increase clot formation. Factor XII deficiencies do not result in increased bleeding risks. Factor V and Factor XIII are involved in creating and maintaining blood clots. Reduced activity of Factor V will reduce clot formation.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Why could the presence of splenomegaly result in thrombocytopenia?

options.html: Thrombopoietin is manufactured by the spleen
Thrombocytes are stored in the spleen
Many clotting factors are stored in the spleen
Antithrombin is produced by the spleen
Antithrombin is stored in the spleen

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Platelets (thrombocytes) are stored in the spleen. Splenomegaly, or enlarged spleen, could result in excessive storing of platelets, reducing availability in the body.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which variant of Heparin would you provide an elderly patient who is at risk of adverse health outcomes and cannot risk an uncertain drug response?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Low molecular weight heparin has a more predictable pharmacokinetic profile, and would provide more predictability of treatment outcomes.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which variant of Heparin would you provide for a patient with kidney disease due to ongoing micro vascular hemorrhage?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

You would not provide an anticoagulant to a patient who is actively bleeding.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following correctly describes the process by which Vitamin K antagonists act as anticoagulants?

options.html: They increase the affinity of antithrombin for thrombin
They deactivate activated factors in the coagulation cascade
They prevent the activation of certain factors in the coagulation cascade
They decrease platelet aggregation in primary hemostasis

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Vitamin K antagonists inhibit Vitamin K reductase which is needed to carboxylate and activate factors II, VII, IX, X.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are treating a patient with a known genetic mutation that impairs antithrombin function. This patient is also noncompliant with his medication often taking too many or too few pills at a time. Which of the following anticoagulants would you prescribe him?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Heparin works by increasing the affinity of antithrombin for thrombin, thus in this patient heparin would be ineffective. A patient who may overdose requires a larger therapeutic window thus direct oral anticoagulants would be the best choice. Warfarin, has many interactions and requires more monitoring.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: For which patient would anticoagulation not be a suitable treatment?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Patients with immune thrombocytopenia have a reduced ability to form blood clots. Administration of anticoagulants for such patients would exacerbate their blood clotting issues.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which option below is a correct antidote to be used for drug reversal?

options.html: An antidote for warfarin is Vitamin B12
An antidote for Dabigatran is idarucizumab
An antidote for Fondaparinux is Factor XII
An antidote for Argatroban is Factor XIII
An antidote for Rivaroxaban is warfarin

answer:
The correct answer is B.

This is the only correct antidote listed. An antidote for warfarin , a vitamin K antagonist, is prothrombin complex concentrate (PCC.. Fondaparinux is an activator of antithrombin. Argatroban is a direct thrombin inhibitor, and Rivaroxaban is a Factor Xa inhibitor.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is a contraindication for Argatroban, an IV-direct thrombin inhibitor?

options.html: A previous history of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia
A patient with elevated thrombin levels
A patient with chronic or acute hepatic failure
A patient with a sizeable gastric resection

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Argatroban is the treatment of choice of patients with a past history of HIT. It is excreted by the liver, so it would not be a good choice for patients with hepatic failure. Argatroban is safe for patients with renal failure. Since it is administered by IV, the presence of a gastric resection would have no effect on the bioavailability of the drug.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient with severe kidney injury presents with reduced platelet counts, normal ADAMTS-13 level, and a peripheral blood smear shows the presence of schistocytes. His coagulation tests INR and PTT are normal. Which of the following diseases are most probable?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome and Thrombotic Thrombocytopenia Purpura both fit with the symptoms in the patient (kidney disease, peripheral blood smear, schistocytes). However kidney disease is more severe in Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome making it more probable, and TTP would be associated with lower levels of ADAMTS-13.) Although DIC can lead to multi-organ dysfunction such as renal failure, the absence of coagulation defects (indicated by normal INR & PTT) makes this unlikely.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following illustrates the correct pathway to confirm a Heparin-Induced Thrombocytopenia?

options.html: Perform a 4T score followed by an ELISA/Serotonin release assay
Perform an ELISA/Serotonin release assay followed by a 4T score
Diagnosis of exclusion rule other causes of thrombocytopenia
ADAMTS-13 level test and presence of schistocytes on blood film

answer:
The correct answer is A.

The 4T test is performed to assess probability of HIT. Based on the results, follow-up tests are necessary. The most diagnostic tests available are the ELISA or serotonin release assay.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem:
Which of the following pathologies can be attributed to decreased production of platelets?

  1. Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP)
  2. Myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS)
  3. Liver disease
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Myelodysplastic syndrome affects the bone marrow which plays a central role in platelet production, the liver secretes thrombopoietin (TPO) which plays a large role in the stimulating platelet production and this process can be impaired by liver disease. Immune Thrombocytopenia is implicated in increased destruction of platelets and decreased production as antibodies can bind to megakaryocytes and decreased production of platelets.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are a hematologist assessing a patient referred for easy bruising. CBC results indicate normal RBCs and WBCs and severe thrombocytopenia. Liver function is normal. A blood film indicates the presence of schistocytes, and subsequent lab tests suggest low levels of ADAMTS-13. He is not taking any medications. What is your recommended treatment?
answer:
The correct answer is E.

With a low ADAMTS-13 level, this patient has thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP). The treatment of choice for TTP is plasma exchange with or without glucocorticoids. Subsequently, rituximab may be added in addition to plasma exchange or used for relapsed disease. TTP is a contraindication for platelets.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient is not taking any medications and presents with thrombocytopenia. Blood tests indicate elevated levels of D-Dimer and low fibrinogen. What is the likely diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

In DIC, there is a systemic activation of all clotting factors, leading to elevated D-Dimer and low fibrinogen. Note that heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (HIT) can also produce clotting (and therefore elevated D-Dimer), but this is unlikely in this case as the patient is not taking any medications.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: After a treatment with low molecular weight heparin (LMWH) such as dalteparin (Fragmin), a patient presents with moderate thrombocytopenia. A 4T score indicates a high probability of HIT, and the diagnosis was confirmed with a serotonin release assay. What is the next course of action?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

With HIT, all heparin-based treatments should be stopped immediately. Warfarin could be a safe alternative after a patient is adequately treated with an alternate anticoagulant (such as argatroban, fondaparinux or danaparoiD. and the platelets have recovered. If used too early as monotherapy, it could cause necrosis as warfarin can lead to low levels of protein C and S that can be prothrombogenic. Platelet transfusions could exacerbate the blood clotting associated with HIT. Argatroban is the most suitable alternative treatment for HIT.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem:
A patient presents with severe Von Willebrand disease where there are inadequate levels of Von Willebrand factor. Which of the following markers/processes would be significantly affected?

  1. Primary hemostasis
  2. Secondary hemostasis
  3. Prothrombin time (PT)
  4. Partial thromboplastin time (PTT)
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Primary Hemostasis would be affected as vWF plays a role in platelet recruitment in formation of the platelet plug. vWF acts as a chaperone for factor VIII extending its halflife, and factor VII plays a central role in the intrinsic pathway of the coagulation cascade measured by PTT. Mild vWD can lead to impaired primary hemostasis. However, with severe vWD as in this case, factor VIII will be reduced and hence PTT will be elevated and secondary hemostasis will be impaired.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following scenarios would warrant a platelet transfusion?

options.html: A patient going for invasive surgery with a low platelet count
A patient with a low platelet count and diagnosed with thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura
A patient with a low platelet count and diagnosed with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia

answer:
The correct answer is A.

TTP and HIT are contraindications for platelet transfusion as the addition of platelets can increase thrombosis without reducing bleeding risk. A patient with hemophilia A would require factor VIII medication, not platelet transfusion.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which transfusion below is safe for all patients if their blood type is unknown?

options.html: Plasma from individuals with Type O- blood
Red blood cells from individuals with Type AB- blood
Red blood cells from individuals with Type O+ blood
Plasma from individuals with Type AB+ blood
Red blood cells from individuals with Type A- blood

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Type O- is the universal RBC donor because the RBCs do not have antigens on the cells. However, Type AB+ plasma does not have any antibodies toward these antigens and is safe for all recipients.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
For the next five questions, choose ONE of the following options for transfusion. Assume

informed consent. Options may be used more than once, or not at all.

stem: A bleeding patient presents with TTP. Platelets are 96 E9/L [normal = 150-400 E9/L]
answer:
The correct answer is C.

First, the patient's platelets are not low enough for platelet transfusion. Second, TTP is a contraindication for platelet transfusion. Plasma is transfused for patients with TTP if plasma exchange is not available.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
For the next five questions, choose ONE of the following options for transfusion. Assume

informed consent. Options may be used more than once, or not at all.

stem: A bleeding patient presents with anemia (Hb = 64 g/L) [normal = 115-160 g/L]
answer:
The correct answer is A.

For severely anemic patients (ie. hemoglobin less than 70 g/L), red blood cells are the best transfusion

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
For the next five questions, choose ONE of the following options for transfusion. Assume

informed consent. Options may be used more than once, or not at all.

stem: A patient requires warfarin anticoagulation reversal.
answer:
The correct answer is E.

Warfarin anticoagulation reversal requires PCC transfusions. Note that this should also be supplemented with Vitamin K.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
For the next five questions, choose ONE of the following options for transfusion. Assume

informed consent. Options may be used more than once, or not at all.

stem: A bleeding patient presents with hypofibrinogenemia.
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Fibrinogen concentrates are the transfusion of choice for patients with afibrinogenemia or hypofibrinogenemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html:
For the next five questions, choose ONE of the following options for transfusion. Assume

informed consent. Options may be used more than once, or not at all.

stem: A bleeding patient presents with acquired hemophilia B.
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Plasma transfusion is an option for patients with single factor deficiencies, such as Hemophilia B (Factor IX) where specific factor replacements are NOT available.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is an incorrect description of the expiry of a type of transfusion?

options.html: Red blood cells can be stored at 4 °C for up to 42 days.
PCC can be stored at room temperature for up to 5 years
Plasma can be stored in a freezer (-18 °C. for up to a year
Platelets can be stored at room temperature for up to 7 days
Cryoprecipitate can be stored at room temperature for up to 5 years

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Cryoprecipitate should be stored in the freezer (-18 °C. and can be stored for up to 1 year.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Von Willebrand deficiency can reduce the half-life of factor VIII in the coagulation cascade. Which of the following markers can be affected in Von Willebrand disease?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Factor VIII is a component of the intrinsic pathway which is measured by the PTT; it is important to note that a normal PTT may not exclude VWD as not all VWD is associated with a low FVIII. Measuring the VW antigen, VW activity and FVIII activity would be pertinent when assessing for VWD.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem:
Which of the following markers would be significantly affected in severe liver disease?

  1. Prothrombin Time (PT)
  2. Partial Thromboplastin Time (PTT)
  3. Platelet count
answer:
The correct answer is D.

The liver produces all the coagulation factors except FVIII (that are involved in both the intrinsic, extrinsic pathway and common pathway), thus the PT,PTT and TT (as fibrinogen can also be low) would be affected. The liver also produces thrombopoietin which stimulates platelet production. Also, chronic liver disease is often associated with portal hypertension and resultant splenomegaly with platelet sequestration.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with Petechiae, wet purpura and bleeding at several mucocutaneous sites. Which of the following causes are most likely for this presentation?

options.html: An impairment in the intrinsic pathway of the coagulation cascade
An impairment in the extrinsic pathway of the coagulation cascade
An impairment in formation of the platelet plug
An impairment in the fibrin cross-linking

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Mucocutaneous (oral cavity, nasal, uterine, skin) sites of bleeding, petechiae, wet purpura, ecchymoses are all signs of defects in primary hemostasis. The formation of the platelet plug occurs during primary hemostasis, while the impairments in the coagulation cascade belong to secondary hemostasis, and fibrin cross-linking is tertiary hemostasis). It is important to note that in clinical practice, it is common to have overlap of presenting symptoms. I.e. patient with mild factor deficiency may present with mucocutaneous bleeding only. Therefore, this question is geared towards having an approach, but it may not be fully explanatory in clinical practice.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Key feature question: Select four answers. In which of the following is an elevated aPTT most likely?

options.html: Patients with deficiency in clotting factor VII
A mixing test performed for patients with a deficiency in clotting factor IX
A mixing test performed for patients with an inhibitor to clotting factor XI
Patients with mutations in clotting factor XIII
Patients with severe von Willebrand’s disease (vWD.

answer:
The correct answer is B, D, E, G.

The aPTT involves the intrinsic coagulation pathway (Factors XII, XI, IX, and VIII). Hemophilia A is associated with Factor VIII; The Lupus anticoagulant is an antibody that targets phospholipids which initiate the intrinsic pathway. vWD has reduced levels of von Willebrand factor (or reduced activity), which is a chaperone protein for Factor VIII. Note that mixing tests can correct deficient clotting factors, but not in the presence of an inhibitor to a clotting factor.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A recent newborn from a homebirth presents with easy bruising, but blood counts (RBCs, WBCs, platelets) are normal. A physical exam is unremarkable, and there are no indications of liver disease or family history for an inherited bleeding disorder. Further testing is performed to elucidate the cause of the bruising. The patient has an elevated INR and prolonged aPTT. Based on the above, which of the following diagnoses are most likely?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Options C, D, and E are associated with elevated aPTT only, and also, factor XII deficiency does not increase bleeding risk! Option A would be associated with elevated PT (or INR) only. In the case of vitamin K deficiency, there are Vitamin K-dependent clotting factors in the intrinsic pathway and the extrinsic pathway, so a severe vitamin K deficiency would elevate both the INR and the aPTT.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following would NOT be significantly lower (relative to an adult) in a newborn?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Factor VIII is actually elevated in the newborn and plays a protective role in bleeding. The liver in children less than 6 months of age are immature and the coagulation factors produced by the liver are in smaller quantities – however factor VIII is not produced by the liver

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following would be most beneficial to treat an undiagnosed coagulopathy?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Fresh frozen plasma is helpful in emergent situations when a factor card (or in this case diagnosis) is not readily available. Fresh frozen plasma contains most factors and fibrinogen.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Tyler is a newborn who bleeds excessively after circumcision. Tyler’s father and paternal grandmother have Hemophilia B. Tyler’s mother and maternal grandfather have von Willebrand disease. Based on this information, what is the most likely diagnosis for Tyler?

options.html: Hemophilia B, because it can be inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern.
Hemophilia B, because it can be inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.
von Willebrand disease, because it can be inherited in an X-linked recessive pattern.
von Willebrand disease, because it can be inherited in an autosomal dominant pattern.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Hemophilia disorders are X-linked, whereas vWD is autosomal (either dominant or recessive depending on the sub-typE.. Note that Tyler could not have inherited an X-linked disorder from his father.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following deficiencies would not lead to a bleeding disorder?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Factor XII is a contact factor affects the aPTT in vitro. It is not significant in vivo and does not present a bleeding risk if there is a deficiency.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You perform a clinical assessment to determine if a patient has DVT, and you conclude that it is unlikely. What is the next best step?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

A negative D-dimer test can be used rule out DVT. If the D-dimer comes test back positive you can use a Compression Ultrasound to diagnose DVT.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You perform a V/Q scan in a patient you suspect has pulmonary embolism. The test results come back as “Non-Diagnostic”. What is the next best step?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

If the test comes out as non-diagnostic, you would then order a bilateral compression ultrasound (on both legs) to determine if they have DVT, as DVT is associated with pulmonary embolism.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with edema in their left leg, associated with pain. You suspect a deep vein thrombosis (DVT). What is the first test you order to diagnose this patient when DVT is likely?
answer:
The correct answer is E.

A positive result for compression ultrasound indicates DVT. A negative result is inconclusive and further testing is necessary.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Based on the Wells criteria, a patient is unlikely to have deep vein thrombosis (DVT) or pulmonary embolism (PE). What statement on subsequent testing is true?

options.html: A positive D-Dimer test confirms DVT.
A negative D-Dimer test leads to additional testing for DVT
A positive D-Dimer test leads to additional testing for PE
A negative D-Dimer test leads to additional testing for PE

answer:
The correct answer is C.

If a patient is unlikely to have DVT or PE based on the Wells criteria, a negative D- Dimer test will rule out DVT or PE. A positive D-Dimer test requires additional testing to arrive at a definitive diagnosis.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A male patient is being treated for a venous thromboembolism. Which statement below on treatment options is true?

options.html: If it was determined that his DVT was idiopathic, his anticoagulant treatment should be continued indefinitely.
For DVT, physical activity is encouraged, but for PE, physical activity is discouraged.
