Patients with elevated INRs should receive higher doses of warfarin.
If the underlying cause of DVT was cancer and the cancer was cured, the patient should continue the treatment for DVT for at least six months after the cancer cure.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

For idiopathic DVTs, anticoagulant treatment is prescribed indefinitely, even after the DVT is addressed.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which abnormal cell morphology is observed in the following blood film?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

The blue structure in the blood film is a Döhle body, which is typically light blue-gray, basophilic, leukocyte inclusion located in the cytoplasm of neutrophil. They are thought to be remnants of the rough endoplasmic reticulum.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient’s CBC-Differential indicates significant eosinophilia with no other leukocytosis. What is the most probable diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Eosinophils target parasites and are involved in the allergic response. However, basophils are also involved in the allergic response. A parasitic infection is likely to increase eosinophil levels only. Additionally, eosinophilia tends to be very mild in allergic response.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following clinical findings is inconsistent with tumour lysis syndrome?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

In tumour lysis syndrome, components inside tumour cells are released into the bloodstream. Since potassium is found in higher concentrations in the cytoplasm, tumour lysis syndrome would result in hyperkalemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 25-year-old patient presents with lymphocytosis. You suspect he is fighting a viral or bacterial infection. Which clinical observation is inconsistent with your working diagnosis?

options.html: The patient has had a fever for a week
Lymphocytes on the peripheral blood smear
Lymphoblasts on the peripheral blood smear

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Viral infections are the most common cause of lymphocytosis. It’s common to see an elevated neutrophil count and lymphocytes in the peripheral blood smear if this patient is fighting a viral/bacterial infection. If the patient had a fever past 4-6 weeks this would be concerning. The presence of lymphoblasts in the peripheral blood smear is not common in infection and can suggest acute lymphoblastic leukemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: Use the following options below to answer the next THREE questions.

stem: A patient presents with basophilia, eosinophilia, and neutrophilia. Their blood film also shows a few immature neutrophils, particularly myelocytes and metamyelocytes. Which of the following conditions best align with this condition?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (a myeloproliferative neoplasm) often presents with these symptoms. While there are immature WBCs in the peripheral blood (left shift), the vast majority of cells are mature which rules out Acute Myeloid Leukemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: Use the following options below to answer the next THREE questions.

stem: A patient’s blood smear shows a significantly elevated level of monoblasts with very few mature macrophages. Which of the following conditions best align with this condition?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Having an elevated level of monoblasts or myeloblasts points to Acute Myeloid Leukemia where myelocytes/monocytes (eosinophils, basophils, neutrophils) have an arrest in maturation.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: Use the following options below to answer the next THREE questions.

stem: A patient presents with an elevated level of mature neutrophils. Cytogenetic and molecular testing were conducted and ruled out any bone marrow pathology. No secondary issue could be identified. Which of the following conditions best align with this condition?
answer:
The correct answer is E.

The lack of bone marrow pathology or secondary causes that can lead to increased neutrophils, points to decreased destruction of neutrophils to explain the elevated count. The spleen plays a large role in the sequestration and destruction of blood cells, thus a reduction in spleen activity can lead to elevated neutrophil counts.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: What is the current standard of care for patients with a t(9,22) translocation leading to chronic myeloid leukemia (BCR-ABL fusion protein)?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Imatinib is an oral inhibitor of the BCR-ABL fusion protein. ATRA and arsenic are treatments for acute promyelocytic leukemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which option correctly describes a treatment option for different leukemias?

options.html: The treatment of CLL is prophylactic chemotherapy immediately after diagnosis
The treatment of CML involves prophylaxis for sanctuary sites such as the CNS and testes
The treatment of ALL is Gleevec / imatinib
The treatment for APL is ATRA
The treatment for AML is Arsenic

answer:
The correct answer is D.

All-trans-retinoic acid (ATRA) and arsenic is the treatment for APL. Imatinib is the treatment for CML. Prophylaxis for sanctuary sites is the treatment for ALL. Note, in CLL, patients are treated only after symptoms develop

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following cells would be significantly altered in acute myeloid leukemia?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Acute leukemia signifies immature blood cells which rules out mature cells (Neutrophils, B- cells) while the myeloid component rules out cells from the lymphoid lineage (lymphoblasts and B-cells)

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: According to the World Health Organization, acute myeloid leukemia is identified by which condition?

options.html: The frequency of blast cells in your peripheral blood
Morphological characteristics of white blood cells

answer:
The correct answer is C.

If you have certain genetic abnormalities regardless of your blast count you have Acute Myeloid Leukemia, according to WHO’s classification system.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 70-year old hospital volunteer requires a blood film examination prior to starting placement. The following blood film is obtained despite the patient feeling entirely well. Which of the following pathologies is most likely?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Most patients with CLL are often asymptomatic in the early stages of the disease. Note: The presence of smudge cells is an artifact in blood films. Often lymphocytes “smudge” easier so conditions such as CLL with lots of lymphocytes will have more “smudge” cells.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: What is not an underlying reason why treatment success rates for ALL in children have increased in the past 30 years?

options.html: Personalized treatments based on risk assessments
Improved ability to provide supportive care during treatment
Increased radiation therapy instead of intrathecal therapy
Post-treatment flow cytometry to assess for residual disease

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Treatments for ALL in children have generally improved for several reasons. One of these is the replacement of radiation therapy with intrathecal therapy.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A child presents with abnormal bruising and bilateral leg pain in the absence of any obvious injuries. Which observation during the physical exam would support a diagnosis of acute myeloid leukemia over acute lymphoid leukemia?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Gingival swelling is indicative of AML in children. Splenomegaly would be observed in both AML and ALL.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following best describes the function of the intensification stage of treatment in pediatric acute lymphoblastic leukemia?

options.html: To induce a remission state in the patient often times using multi-agent chemotherapy
Treat the remaining microscopic cancer to overcome resistance often using moderate intensive chemotherapy
To continue the remission of the patient and maintain a cancer free state
To prevent the infiltration of leukemia into the CNS or other organs

answer:
The correct answer is B.

The Intensification stage is conducted after the patient reaches a remission state and is done to treat any lingering cancer cells.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient with intracerebral hemorrhage presents with abnormal fibrinolysis activity and disseminated intravascular coagulation. A peripheral blood smear from the patient is shown below. Which leukemia would best explain these symptoms?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Patients with Acute promyelocytic leukemia (APL), a type of Acute Myeloid Leukemia (AML), often present with increased fibrinolytic activity, disseminated intravascular coagulation and have a high risk of hemorrhage relative to other types of AML. Also, the presence of multiple Auer rods within myeloblasts and increased promyelocytes are characteristic of APL.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which diagnostic technique cannot be performed on a bone marrow aspirate?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

A pathological assessment is performed on a bone marrow biopsy. Flow cytometry can be performed on bone marrow aspirate and peripheral blood.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Key feature question: Select two answers. A new patient arrives with erythrocytosis. You conduct a thorough patient history and some lab tests. Which two statements are inconsistent with a secondary erythrocytosis?

options.html: The patient recently climbed Mount Everest
The patient has low erythropoietin levels
The patient has obstructive sleep apnea
The patient smoked 1.5 packs per day for the last 20 years
The patient has a mutation on exon 12 of JAK2
The patient is a competitive marathon runner and partakes in EPO doping

answer:
The correct answer is C, F.

These statements are consistent with a primary erythrocytosis. Activities in the patient’s history which lead to an elevated erythrocyte count (high altitude, EPO doping, reduced oxygen intake due to smoking or OSA).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: What is a correct description of the etiology of polycythemia vera?

options.html: The bone marrow no longer responds to erythropoietin and erythropoiesis is halted.
The kidneys no longer produce erythropoietin and erythropoiesis is halted.
The kidneys produce extra erythropoietin and erythropoiesis is upregulated.
Erythropoiesis continues in the absence of erythropoietin
Hypoxia in the kidneys increases the production of erythropoietin

answer:
The correct answer is D.

In polycythemia vera, the kidneys continue to produce erythropoietin even in the absence of erythropoietin. This is caused by a mutation in JAK2 (JAK2 V617F, or exon 12 mutation) which constitutively expresses JAK2 signaling.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A new patient presents to your clinic with hypertension and headache, and the CBC indicates panmyelosis despite low levels of erythropoietin. Cytogenetic testing is positive for a JAK2 V617F mutation. You assess that the patient is at high risk for thrombosis. What is your immediate and long-term treatment respectively?

options.html: Aspirin and referral to Canadian Blood Services for blood donation
Heparin and watchful waiting for worsening symptoms
Treat the underlying anemia with O- red blood cells
Treat the underlying cause of secondary erythrocytosis and repeat CBC after the condition resolves.

answer:
The correct answer is A.

For patients with high-risk erythrocytosis, aspirin is immediately taken to reduce DVT risk, and cytoreduction via hydroxyurea is a long-term treatment. Note that phlebotomy is a suitable treatment for low-risk patients. Phlebotomy could be appropriate for a high-risk patient, but hydroxyurea is necessary to rapidly decrease hemoglobin. The presence of the JAK2 mutation indicates a primary erythrocytosis, so E is false.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following diagnostic tests would NOT be appropriate for a patient that presents with erythrocytosis?

options.html: Testing for a JAK2 V617F mutation for a patient with low EPO
Conducting an echocardiogram for a patient with low EPO
Conducting a pulmonary function test for a patient with high EPO
Conducting a sleep study for a patient with high EPO

answer:
The correct answer is B.

An echocardiogram is offered for patients with a high EPO who have secondary erythrocytosis (no BM pathology); this can be used to see if there are shunts in the heart which misdirect blood from entering the lungs to be oxygenated thus leading to hypoxia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: Use the following options to answer the next FOUR questions.

stem: A patient’s blood sample is taken and when centrifuged the hematocrit is large and the buffy layer is normal. Which pathology best explains this result?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

In Secondary Erythrocytosis the patient is producing higher quantities of erythrocytes which would explain the elevated hematocrit. However the white blood cells and the platelets (which make up the buffy layer) are unaffected.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: Use the following options to answer the next FOUR questions.

stem: A patient’s blood sample is taken and when centrifuged the hematocrit is large and the buffy layer is large. Which pathology best explains this result?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

In Primary Erythrocytosis there is often an acquired genetic mutation that leads to panmyelosis (where RBC, WBC and platelet counts are elevated). Thus the hematocrit and the buffy layer would both be proportionally larger.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: Use the following options to answer the next FOUR questions.

stem: A patient’s blood sample is taken and when centrifuged the hematocrit is normal and the buffy layer is large. Which pathology best explains this result?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

In chronic myeloid Leukemia there is an overproduction (abnormal growth) of myeloid lineage granulocytes (eosinophil, basophils, neutrophils). These would lead to a larger buffy layer.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: Use the following options to answer the next FOUR questions.

stem: A patient’s blood sample is taken and when centrifuged the hematocrit is low and the buffy layer is small. Which pathology best explains this result?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

In aplastic anemia there is reduced cellularity of the bone marrow and there is a significant reduction in the production of all blood cells (erythrocytes and leukocytes) which leads to a low hematocrit and low buffy layer.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 15-year-old male presents to a walk-in clinic concerned about a new fever suspecting an infection. On visual examination, there are patches of hyperpigmentation on his back and there are defects in the fingernails. When the CBC results come back, the patient has low erythrocytes, low thrombocytes, and low leukocytes. What is the likely diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Dyskeratosis congenita is a hereditary disorder that can lead to aplastic anemia, characterized by pancytopenia, hyperpigmentation of the skin, fingernail defects, and additionally, leukoplakia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with polydactyly and eye and ear defects. A CBC+ differential shows pancytopenia and a bone marrow core biopsy shows reduced cellularity. Which of the following pathologies fit best with the symptoms and lab findings?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

The reduced cellularity within the bone marrow coupled with the pancytopenia point towards aplastic anemia. Fanconi Anemia is a hereditary disorder that can lead to Aplastic Anemia and is associated with eye and ear defects and polydactyly (extra finger or thumb).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which option below is not considered a myeloproliferative neoplasm?
answer:
The correct answer is E.

Dyskeratosis congenita is a hereditary disorder that can lead to aplastic anemia, which is not considered a myeloproliferative neoplasm.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Myelofibrosis is characterized by the presence of mutations in CALR, JAK2, and MPL. Which of these genes is a mutation most commonly associated with myelofibrosis?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Most mutations leading to myelofibrosis are caused by JAK2 mutations [50-60%].

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 60-year-old patient presents with pancytopenia and an enlarged spleen. Upon taking a peripheral blood smear the following image is obtained. Which of the following pathologies best fit this patient?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

In patients with myelofibrosis there is fibrosis of the bone marrow leading to pancytopenia. There is an excess maturation of myeloid progenitors including granulocytes and erythroid progenitors spilling out into the peripheral blood leading to the leukoerythroblastic picture. The presence of teardrop cells is also seen in Myelofibrosis.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following statements regarding the natural progression of myeloproliferative neoplasms is INCORRECT?

options.html: Patients with Myelofibrosis can be at risk of developing Acute Myeloid Leukemia
Patients with Essential Thrombocythemia can be at risk of developing Myelofibrosis
Patients with Essential Thrombocythemia can be at risk of developing Acute Myeloid Leukemia
Patients with Acute Myeloid Leukemia can be at risk of developing Polycythemia vera

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Patients with Polycythemia vera are at risk of developing Acute Myeloid Leukemia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 24-year-old female comes into your family practice with chronic fatigue. A CBC test reveals leukocytosis. The blood film results are shown below. Based on the results, you suspect acute promyelocytic anemia. What test result would confirm your suspected diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

APL is the result of a translocation of chromosomes 15 and 17 leading to a fusion of the PML/RAR-alpha genes. This can be diagnosed through karyotype, FISH or by molecular genetics testing.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: When a patient presents with secondary thrombocytosis, which reactive (or secondary) condition is unlikely?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Thrombopoietin is produced by the liver. Acute liver disease would result in thrombocytopenia. The rest of the answers would lead to thrombocytosis.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem:
A patient’s lab findings are suggestive of thrombocytosis. Which of the following options can potentially explain this lab finding?

  1. The patient is experiencing inflammation and tissue damage
  2. The patient is positive for the Philadelphia chromosome
  3. The patient’s blood also contains red blood cell fragments
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Inflammation and tissue damage within the body can lead to stimulated production of platelets by the bone marrow (secondary thrombocytosis). Patients who are positive for the Philadelphia chromosome have Chronic Myeloid Leukemia where they can have either thrombocytosis or thrombocytopenia.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following cancer drug classifications would Microtubule Inhibiting Drugs fall under?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Microtubule Inhibiting Drugs inhibit microtubule activity during the M phase of the cellcycle, preventing cancerous cells from further dividing. These drugs are cell-cycle specific as they primarily function in the M phase.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following best describes the mechanism by which the cancer drug Bevacizumab impairs tumour angiogenesis?

options.html: It acts as an antibody which binds Vascular endothelial Growth Factor and prevents its interaction its receptors
It acts as a small molecule inhibitor that enters the cell and leads to the downregulation of VEGF receptors on the cell surface
It acts as an antagonist by binding to VEGF receptors and preventing the VEGF- VEGF receptor interaction
It acts as a CDK inhibitor to prevent cell progression from the G1 to S phase

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Bevacizumab acts as an antibody (most antibody drugs end with –MAB) that bind to VEGF and prevent it from binding to its receptor thereby preventing tumour angiogenesis.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Targeted therapy is a means to treat cancer. Which option demonstrates a true mechanism of action of a targeted cancer therapy treatment?

options.html: Aromatase inhibitors block the conversion of estrogen to androgen.
Drugs that target VEGF receptors halt angiogenesis.
Some cancer cells inhibit CDKs, and CDKs halt the cell-cycle progression.
Drugs that target estrogen receptors increase the proliferation rates of non- cancer cells.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

The VEGF (vascular endothelial growth factor) binds to receptors to stimulate angiogenesis. Drugs can prevent this by targeting the VEGF receptors. For option A, Aromatase inhibitors block the conversion of androgens to estrogens. For option C, CDKs promote cell cycle progression. For Option D, Drugs that target estrogen receptors do not increase the proliferation rates of non-cancer cells, but reduce the proliferation rates of cancer cells.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient is currently on immunotherapy. Which of the following drugs amplify the T cell response via an interaction between T cells and antigen presenting cells?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

CTLA-4 inhibitors bind to the CTLA-4 protein on tumour cells and prevent interaction with B7 (found on antigen presenting cells) which allows the T cells to mount a more robust response). PD-L1 inhibitors work by binding to PD-L1 on tumour cells, preventing PD-1 (found on T cells) from binding to PD-L1 and allows for the killing of the tumour cell.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Key feature question: A patient with a neutrophil count of 0.2 E9/L presents at the emergency department with a fever of 39 °C. What are the best three treatments?
answer:
The correct answer is A, C.

When a patient presents with febrile neutropenia (low WBC count with a fever), the infection and is considered an oncologic emergency. The patient is immediately placed on broad-spectrum antibiotics.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Key feature question: Which two leukocyte sub-types are not considered granulocytes?
answer:
The correct answer is C, D.

Lymphocytes and monocytes are agranulocytes. Basophils, eosinophils, and neutrophils are granulocytes.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is considered the main complication of leukopenia?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Leukopenia is having a reduced number of WBCs – often neutrophils. Without an adequate titer of neutrophils, the body is unable to fight off infection. Leukostasis is often seen in patients with a very high white cell count due to conditions such as acute myeloid leukemia where there is an abundance of immature blasts. Bleeding risk would be associated with a reduction in platelet count/function.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A randomized, double-blind control study took place to determine the efficacy of a new drug, miterbitinib in patients with terminal, incurable, pancreatic cancer. 1000 patients received placebo treatment, and 1000 patients received miterbitinib. At the end of six months, 950 patients receiving placebo died, whereas 900 patients receiving miterbitinib died. In this study, what is the number needed to treat (NNT) to avoid death after 6 months? Assume perfect adherence to the treatment regimen for all 2000 individuals.
answer:
The correct answer is D.

The absolute risk of death at 6 months with placebo and miterbitinib are 0.95 and 0.90, respectively (or, in other words, absolute survival is 0.05 vs 0.10 at 6 months). The absolute risk reduction in death is 0.05 (0.95-0.90). The NNT is calculated by 1/ARR, and 1/0.05 = 20. This means that, on average, treating 20 people with miterbitinib avoids 1 death after six months.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which statement on the topic of critical appraisal is true?

options.html: Bias reduces the precision of a study’s findings.
Equipoise dictates that it is only ethical to conduct clinical trials in areas of uncertainty.
Confounding can be avoided completely in a randomized control trial.
A per protocol analysis studies individuals based on the protocol they were assigned.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Precision is a term that generally refers to ‘standard error’. Standard error can be reduced with large sample size but the study can still be inaccurate if there is bias. Bias is systematic error that leads to INACCURATE results rather than imprecise results. Randomized control trials are designed to reduce confounding but may not completely eliminate it. Per-protocol analysis (also known as on-treatment analysis) involves analyzing according to the treatment actually received and completed by the individuals – those who adhered to the protocol.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A drug pharmaceutical company has made an alternative to the cancer drug Bevacizumab, with the primary intention being to reduce the accompanying nausea and discomfort with the original drug. Their hope is that this drug is not less efficacious than Bevacizumab. Which of the following trials are best suited for this alternative?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

A non-inferiority trial is designed to assess if a drug is not less efficacious than the standard therapy, and this would be the design of choice to ensure the alternative is not less efficacious than Bevacizumab. A superiority trial is designed to assess if a drug is more efficacious than the standard therapy. An equivalence trial is designed to show that a drug is no more efficacious and no less efficacious than the standard therapy.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is NOT a valid reason to prefer the “Intention to Treat Analysis” over the “Per-Protocol Analysis”?

options.html: Intention to treat analysis is more like the “real world”
With the Per Protocol analysis, exclusions of non-adhering patients can introduce a bias
With the Per Protocol analysis, if too many patients are excluded the sample size can be reduced and thereby reduce study power
Intention to treat analysis is generally more likely to capture a greater treatment effect

answer:
The correct answer is D.

Intention to treat analysis is more likely to register a treatment effect that is too conservative because of non-adherence by patients enrolled in therapy group

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following characteristics of lymphadenopathies is NOT characteristic of a malignancy?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Non-tender nodes are usually indicative of a malignancy.

Sexually transmitted infection

preamble.html: Use the following answers to answer the next THREE questions.

stem: A patient has a mediastinal lymphadenopathy, which cause is most likely?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Tuberculosis

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 15-year-old presents to your family practice with a lymphadenopathy of the submandibular area. The patient history is suggestive of a bacterial infection. What is your best course of action? Select two answers.
answer:
The correct answer is A, D.

Since the lymphadenopathy is likely to be caused by an infection, the infection should be treated. The follow-up is meant to confirm that treatment worked and confirm that something more sinister like lymphoma is not causing the enlarged lymph node.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient is concerned about a suspicious lump in their supraclavicular region. What aspect of the patient’s history decreases the likelihood of the lump being neoplastic?

options.html: The patient has been having drenching night sweats.
The patient has rapid unexplained weight loss.
The patient has a 40 pack-year smoking history.
The patient’s lump has been present for 7 days.
The patient has a family history of early onset breast cancer.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

The sudden onset of lymphadenopathy indicates that infection or inflammation is a more likely cause. Drenching night sweats and unexplained weight loss are B-symptoms and indicate neoplasm, and a past history of smoking plus a family history of early onset cancer indicates an increased likelihood for cancer.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 50-year-old woman presents with a suspected malignancy. A CT scan shows a mass in her anterior mediastinum. Which of the following pathologies is at the top of your differential diagnosis?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Thymoma is the most prevalent tumour in the anterior mediastinum for women in that age group. Hodgkin’s lymphoma is more common in younger women (ages 10-39). An esophageal tumour would be interpreted as mass in the middle mediastinum and a thoracic spine lesion would be interpreted as a mass in the posterior mediastinum.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following structures are found in the middle compartment of the mediastinum?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

The thymus is located in the anterior compartment, and the spine, esophagus, and thoracic aorta are located in the posterior compartment.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient presents with a positive Pemberton’s sign. Which statement below is true?

options.html: A mass may be obstructing their inferior vena cava
A mass may be obstructing their superior vena cava
A mass may have severed their inferior vena cava
A mass may have severed their superior vena cava

answer:
The correct answer is B.

The Pemberton’s sign is associated with an obstruction of the superior vena cava.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 50 year old patient presents to your clinic for a periodic health encounter. The patient describes shortness of breath, cough and difficulty swallowing. Upon further examination you also notice this patient has one constricted pupil and one dilated pupil, and one of their eyelids is drooping. Which of the following conditions is a likely cause for the signs and symptoms?

options.html: Superior Vena Cava Obstruction from a mediastinal mass
Horner’s syndrome from a mediastinal mass
Laryngeal Nerve compression from a mediastinal mass
Vagus Nerve compression from a mediastinal mass

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Horner’s syndrome is characterized by miosis (constricted pupil), partial ptosis drooping of eyelid) and anhidrosis (inability to sweat), and oftentimes this occurs unilaterally in the body. SVC obstruction would present as edema in the face and neck and would be accompanied by Pemberton’s Sign. The Laryngeal Nerve innervates the larynx and affects the patient’s ability to speak and the Vagus Nerve (a parasympathetic nerve) innervates visceral organs of the cardiovascular, pulmonary and digestive system.)

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: What is the most common cause of lymphadenopathy?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

Infection is by far the most common cause of lymphadenopathy.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is an accurate difference between lymph nodes and the spleen?

options.html: The lymph node contains follicles whereas the spleen does not
Lymph node receives afferent lymphatics where the spleen has an afferent blood supply
The spleen contains antigen presenting cells where the lymph node does not
The lymph nodes can swell due to an infection whereas the spleen does not

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Lymph nodes and the spleen both contain follicles (germinal center, marginal zone, mantle layer). Both contain antigen presenting cells. The lymph nodes and the spleen (splenomegaly) can be enlarged during an infection. The spleen contains an afferent blood supply whereas the lymph nodes contain afferent lymphatics.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following techniques is most valuable in terms of diagnostic ability for biopsying a lymph node?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Surgical excision where the entire lymph node is extracted is invasive however provides the most diagnostic yield. Core needle biopsy is better for diagnostic purposes than Fine Needle Aspiration which has a high false negative rate. Punch Biopsy is only used for skin lesions and not appropriate for lymph nodes.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You are performing a lymph node biopsy for a patient you suspect to have Hodgkin’s lymphoma. Which of the following principles do you use to perform this biopsy?

options.html: Select the most superficial lymph node to minimize the invasiveness of the procedure.
With surgical excision, remove a small part of the lymph node as opposed to the whole lymph node.
Select the largest lymph node as this contains the most tissue for diagnostic purposes
Excise a large lymph node and a smaller lymph node to compare diagnostically.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Many of the superficial lymph nodes are often benign or atypical, however the deeper and larger lymph nodes are better suited for diagnostic purposes. The larger the lymph node the more likely it is to contain diagnostic tissue.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A pathologist receives an excised lymph node for pathologic investigation. Using immunohistochemical staining, the pathologist noted a region rich in T-cells. Based on the location of these T-cells, the pathologist concluded that the lymph node was completely normal. Where were these T-cells?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

T-cells are rich in the interfollicular region, but sparse in the germinal center, mantle zone, and marginal zone.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A pathologist examined a lymph node sample but based on sample size, could not rule out lymphoma as a diagnosis. What sampling technique did the pathologist likely receive?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

A FNA has reduced diagnostic ability, but is sometimes used as a first diagnostic technique because of its non-invasive nature and low cost.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following flow cytometry findings is NOT characteristic of a malignancy?

options.html: B-lymphocytes that are monoclonal (express either kappa or lambda light chains)
B-lymphocytes that are polyclonal (express both kappa and lambda light chains)
B-lymphocytes that express CD5 (which is commonly found on T cells)
B-lymphocytes that lose their normal CD markers (CD19, CD20)

answer:
The correct answer is B.

B lymphocytes that are polyclonal are benign. It is worth noting that in Hodgkin lymphoma, the flow cytometry shows a polyclonal pattern, as there are too few ReedSternberg cells to be detected by flow.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: You suspect a patient has a malignancy and biopsy a lymph node. A histological sample from the biopsied lymph node is shown below. How would you classify this patient’s pathology?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Hodgkin lymphoma is characterized by Reed-Sternberg cells with a binucleate cell.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which option below INCORRECTLY differentiates Hodgkin lymphoma (HL) from nonHodgkin lymphoma (NHL)?

options.html: Reed-Sternberg cells are only observed in HL, never in NHL.
NHL can spread contiguously or non-contiguously, HL usually spreads contiguously.
HL cannot be detected by flow cytometry but NHL can.
NHL is more common than HL.
Patients with NHL have better prognoses than patients with HL.

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Hodgkin Lymphoma is treatable and often curable. Non-Hodgkin lymphoma is treatable and some subtypes are curable but not all of them are.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.

preamble.title: Shared instructions
preamble.html: The next three questions relate to the same clinical case scenario.

stem: A 25-year-old male patient presents with several enlarged lymph nodes in the supraclavicular region. The patient remarked feeling easily fatigued, with mild shortness of breath upon physical activity, and bloating. He denied fever, weight loss or night sweats. An excisional biopsy reveals the patient has Hodgkin Lymphoma. Subsequent PET-CT scans indicate that the lymphoma is limited to his supraclavicular lymph nodes, axillary lymph nodes, a small mediastinal mass, and abdominal lymph nodes. What is the stage of the patient?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

The patient’s Lymphoma is stage IIIA. He has more than two nodal areas affected, both above and below the level of the diaphragm. There is no extra-nodal involvement indicated by the PETCT scan, and in addition, the patient has not reported any B-symptoms.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following treatments would you suggest to the 25-year-old patient?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

ABVD chemotherapy is the first line treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma, which is highly responsive to both radiation and chemotherapy. CHOP-R is used in diffuse B cell lymphoma. Radiation alone is not standard treatment for Hodgkin lymphoma, but is sometimes used after chemotherapy (in limited stage HL or if there is a persistently PET positive lesion after chemo). Watch and wait is used for asymptomatic patients with incurable lymphomas such as follicular lymphoma. Surgical excision is not a treatment for lymphoma.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: The 25-year-old patient completes their recommended treatment. Which of the following techniques would is most appropriate when reassessing the patient for residual lymphoma?

options.html: Physical exam to palpate lymph nodes

answer:
The correct answer is C.

A PET scan is better at assessing for residual active tumor than a CT scan or MRI; CT scan or MRI cannot distinguish tumors from residual scar tissue, whereas PET scans can. A PET scan is appropriate as it determines which regions are consuming radiolabeled fluorodeoxyglucose more rapidly (tumours use glucose faster than normal tissues).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which option below correctly describes a potential treatment option for lymphoma?

options.html: Chemotherapy (CHOP-R) cannot be followed by radiation due to adverse effects.
Stem cell treatments are not used because there is not enough evidence of efficacy.
“Watch and wait” is used for slow-growing, incurable non-Hodgkin-lymphomas.
Immune therapy is only available for lymphomas involving polyclonal B-cells.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

When a lymphoma is slow-growing and cannot be cured, watch and wait is the best strategy for treatment. Chemotherapy can be followed by radiation therapy, usually after a short break. Stem cell treatments can be used to treat lymphoma. Immune therapy involves monoclonal antibody drugs that target B-cells. Rituximab (the “R” in CHOP-R) is a monoclonal antibody used in the treatment for non-Hodgkin lymphoma, which is a monoclonal B-cell lymphoma. Specifically, rituximab targets the antigen CD20, found on B- cells.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient with known lymphoma has several affected lymph nodes. The areas affected are the supraclavicular region, the mediastinal region, and the inguinal region. A PET/CT reveals extra-nodal spread to the kidneys. On patient history and examination, he denies night sweats and any recent weight loss. He has been experiencing intermittent fevers up to 38.5 °C. Based on the above, what is the most likely type of lymphoma and what stage of lymphoma does this patient have? Select TWO answers.
answer:
The correct answer is A, H.

The non-contiguous spread of the lymphoma is more in keeping with non-Hodgkin Lymphoma, though it does not totally exclude Hodgkin lymphoma. This patient has nodal involvement both above and below the diaphragm and extra-nodal involvement, signifying Stage IV. Based on the presence of at least one B-symptom (fever), the patient is Stage IVB.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A 40-year-old patient presents asymptomatically with bilateral axillary and supraclavicular lymphadenopathy. There are no other sites of disease. A biopsy confirms follicular lymphoma and blood work confirms a normal LDH level and a Hemoglobin of 130 g/L (normal). With regards to the Follicular Lymphoma International Prognostic Index (FLIPI), which risk group does the patient fall into?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

The patient does not have any risk factors. Her lymphoma involves less than 4 nodal areas, she is below 60 years of age, her stage is 2 (axillary and supraclavicular nodes are both above the diaphragm) and her LDH and hemoglobin levels are normal.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following treatment options is most appropriate for the 40-year-old patient in the previous question?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

This patient is presenting asymptomatically with stage II follicular lymphoma so observation is appropriate. If the patient was stage I, radiation would be recommended. If a patient had stage II+ and was symptomatic BR chemotherapy would be the first line chemotherapy option. ABVD chemotherapy is used for Hodgkin lymphoma.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following correctly describes a process by which fractionation helps in radiation therapy?

options.html: Fractionation allows healthy cells to reoxygenate between radiation doses which will impair DNA repair.
Fractionation leads surrounding cells to exit the cell cycle and stop proliferating, halting tumour growth.
Fractionation allows tumour cells to reoxygenate between radiation doses, which makes the treatment more lethal.
Fractionation allows tumours to repair themselves in an incorrect manner leading to their own death.

answer:
The correct answer is C.

Reoxygenation of hypoxic cells makes them more sensitive to radiation, and when radiation is fractionated cancerous cells are able to reoxygenate. Reoxygenation does not help with repair in healthy cells. Fractionating the radiation doses thereby providing time between doses allows cancer cells to enter a more sensitive stage of the cell cycles and become more susceptible to radiation.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient is scheduled for radiation therapy for a lymphoma in their neck and head region. Which of the following is LEAST likely to be a side effect?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Side effects during radiation therapy are often localized to the site of radiation. You would not expect shortness of breath unless radiation was administered to the chest region.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Britney Spears has lymphoma and requires a modest dose of radiation therapy to her bilateral neck and larynx spread out over 20 daily sessions. Which treatment modality would be used?
answer:
The correct answer is A.

Lymphoma is almost never treated with SABR because the microscopic area of the spread is too broad for a tiny target. Furthermore, the doses required for lymphoma are too modest to be appropriate for SABR. The treatment modality for lymphoma is external beam radiation.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Key feature question: On the subject of radiation oncology, which two statements below are true?

options.html: Large radiation doses are broken down into several smaller doses spread out over a longer period of time – this process is called fractionation.
Brachytherapy involves the use of a linear decelerator to slowly administer radiation.
In radiation therapy, the ultimate goal is for the cancer cells to die but for normal cells to self-repair.
The side-effects of radiation therapy are often immediately apparent.
Radiation therapy is used for cancer cure, but the toxic side-effects make it a poor choice for palliative care.

answer:
The correct answer is A, C.

Brachytherapy involves decaying radioactive isotopes placed near the tumour. Sideeffects of radiation treatment typically manifest near the end of the treatment regimen. Lastly, radiation therapy is used with curative and palliative intent.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: A patient’s blood test shows the presence of Monoclonal protein (M Protein). The physician conducts a bone marrow biopsy and notices the bone marrow contains 15% plasma cells. The patient is not reporting any symptoms. Which stage best fits the patient's description?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Smoldering multiple myeloma is characterized as asymptomatic, bone marrow is more than 10% plasma cell and the presence of Protein M in urine or blood samples.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following is NOT a symptom of Multiple Myeloma?

options.html: Anemia due to bone marrow infiltration from plasma cells
Hypocalcemia due to increased osteoclast activity
Renal failure from elevated levels of M protein
Increased risk of infection from neutropenia

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Osteoclast activity is increased due to inflammatory cytokines produced by plasma cells, which consequently leads to bone reabsorption and higher serum calcium (hypercalcemia).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following tests could be performed to identify a patient with MGUS or smoldering Myeloma?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Protein Electrophoresis would identify the presence of a Monoclonal protein (M protein) from a urine or blood sample. Patients with MGUS and smoldering Myeloma are asymptomatic thus it is unlikely to find significant findings such as neutropenia, anemia (from a CBC) or reduced bone density (from a skeletal survey) or kidney dysfunction (from renal function tests).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which lab test results and their respective indications help in the diagnosis of multiple myeloma? Select TWO answers.

options.html: Elevated calcium levels indicating bone lesions
Reduced creatinine levels indicating impaired renal function
Pancytopenia indicating reduced bone marrow infiltration
Rouleaux cells in the blood film indicating presence of M-protein
X-ray, CT, or PET-CT indicating elevated osteoblast activity

answer:
The correct answer is A, D.

Impaired renal function results in elevated creatinine levels. Pancytopenia is the result of increased bone marrow infiltration. In multiple myeloma, increased osteoclast activity results in bone lesions.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the patients below is most likely to have plasma cell leukemia?

options.html: A patient with renal damage and anemia, with 15% monoclonal plasma cells in the bone marrow.
A patient with renal damage and bone lesions with 25% monoclonal plasma cells in the peripheral blood.
An asymptomatic patient with 15% monoclonal plasma cells in the bone marrow.
An asymptomatic patient with 7% monoclonal plasma cells in the bone marrow.
A patient with depositions of insoluble M-protein in organs and other tissues.

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Plasma cell leukemia is characterized as symptomatic with end organ damage and plasma cells in the peripheral blood (>20%).

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: 5-Fluorouracil is a chemotherapy agent which works by inhibiting the production of thymine within tumour (and non-cancerous) cells. Which of the following is the best classification of this drug?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Antimetabolites interfere with the normal cellular metabolism of nucleic acids.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Zevalin is a chemotherapy agent used in relapsed follicular lymphoma. Zevalin is unique in that it is an antibody that also delivers radiation. Which of the following is the best classification of this drug?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Conjugated monoclonal antibodies contain an attachment to the antibody which contains additional therapeutic properties.

lectureMeta: The student-written, instructor-approved bank built by the Class of 2024 Academic Directors (December 2020) and re-filed per week by the Meds 2025 volunteers.
stem: Which of the following drugs would be used to treat chronic lymphocytic leukemia?

options.html: Bruton Kinase Inhibitor (interferes in B cell antigen receptor signaling)
ATRA/Arsenic (allows cells to differentiate into mature granulocytes)
Imatinib (inhibits constitutive activity of BCR-Abl receptor through competitive inhibition)

answer:
The correct answer is A.

Bruton Kinase Inhibitor is used to treat CLL, as it interferes in signaling that is necessary for B cell tumour expansion. ATRA/Arsenic is used to treat Acute Promyelocytic Leukemia. Imatinib is used to treat Chronic Myeloid Leukemia. Velcade is used to treat multiple myeloma.

Brandon, who is receiving 5-fluorouracil (a fluoropyrimidine) and has loss-of function mutations in both of his copies of the gene encoding dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase. (Dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase metabolizes 5-fluorouracil)

Charlie, who is receiving azathioprine (a thiopurine) but has loss-of-function mutations in both of his copies of the gene encoding thiopurine methyltransferase. (Thiopurine methyltransferase metabolizes thiopurines)
David, who is receiving warfarin treatment but has SNPs in both of the genes encoding Vitamin K Epoxide Reductase (VKOR). Specifically, his SNPs increase his VKOR sensitivity to warfarin.

The correct answer is A.

Clopidogrel is a pro-drug that needs to be metabolized into a pharmacologically active metabolite. Reduced metabolism of clopidogrel through mutated CYP2C19 enzymes will result in a smaller response to standard treatment doses.

stem: For which of the following patients would you administer low molecular weight heparin rather than unfractionated heparin (select all that apply)?

options.html: 76M diagnosed with diabetes and acute renal failure
87F who is mostly being cared for outpatient
24F who’s may or may not have taken a significant amount of aspirin prior to hospital admission

answer:
The correct answer is B, D.

LMWH is mostly cleared by the kidney while UFH is mostly cleared by the liver. LMWH can be given subcutaneously, and therefore administered at home, while UFH is given IV and must be administered by a healthcare professional. Aspirin is an anticoagulant and UFH is better revered (with protamine suphate) compared to LMWH. UFH requires extensive PTT monitoring (which requires blood draws) while LMWH does not need to be monitored.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: Which of the following is NOT a cause of an isolated elevated PTT?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

An isolated elevated PTT indicates something is wrong with the intrinsic pathway of the coagulation cascade. Von Willebrand protein acts as a chaperone for FVIII, a part of the intrinsic pathway. Lupus anticoagulant acts as an antiphospholipid antibody, which prevents the activation of the coagulation cascade. Hemophilia A is an autosomal RECESSIVE condition resulting in dysfunctional FVIII. FXI is a part of the intrinsic pathway. Disseminated intravascular coagulation (DIC) will consume all coagulation factors, so their levels will all fall and result in both an elevated PTT and INR.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: A patient presents with a history of heavy bilateral epistaxis that takes 30+ mins to resolve. Which of the following is LEAST likely to be the cause?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Ehlers Danlos syndrome is a connective tissue disease and vascular disorder. Hypersplenism will result in sequestration of platelets and reduce the number of circulating platelets. Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) causes increased destruction of platelets and will reduce the number of circulating platelets. Antiplatelet drugs could either reduce the function of platelets or reduce the number of circulating platelets. These are all examples of problems that affect primary hemostasis. Hemophilia B is an X-linked recessive condition resulting in dysfunction FIX, a part of the intrinsic coagulation cascade. This is an example of a problem that affects secondary hemostasis. Recurrent heavy bilateral epistaxis is a type of mucosal bleed that is more commonly seen in those with dysfunctional primary hemostasis.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: Which of the following is the LEAST likely to indicate a patient may have an underlying bleeding disorder?

options.html: Papercut that takes 20 minutes to stop bleeding

answer:
The correct answer is B.

Menorrhagia is a common condition in otherwise healthy individuals. The presence of menorrhagia alone does not indicate that an individual has an underlying bleeding disorder. Heavy bleeding after dental work, weekly bilateral epistaxis, hemarthrosis, and slow/delayed hemostasis alone also do not indicate that an individual has an underlying bleeding disorder. However, these events are much less common than menorrhagia in healthy individuals, so they are more likely to represent an underlying bleeding disorder.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: A concerned mother brings her 2-month-old son to your walk-in clinic. Her son has had his third nosebleed in the past 2 weeks and she is very worried. She did not have any prenatal screening performed. You suspect an underlying bleeding disorder. Which of the following would NOT be helpful investigations?

options.html: Collect a family history of bleeding
Ask whether or not her son was circumcised and if there has been any associated bleeding
Examine the son’s joints, particularly the ankles and knees
Inquire about the son’s dental work and if there has been any associated bleeding

answer:
The correct answer is D.

It is highly unlikely that a 2-month-old will have had any dental work done. A family history of bleeding may indicate a possible hereditary bleeding disorder. Post-surgical bleeding, such as post-circumcision bleeding, may point towards an underlying bleeding disorder. Identification of hemarthroses and petechiae, purpura, or ecchymoses also may suggest the son has a bleeding disorder.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: Which of the following is FALSE regarding hemostasis in neonates?

options.html: FIX is often significantly lower in neonates and can mimic Hemophilia B
aPTT is greater in neonates compared to adults
Inadequate vitamin K prophylaxis can result in hemorrhagic disease of the newborn
Hemarthroses are uncommon in neonates with hemophilia up until the 6-8 month mark
Neonates typically have lower levels of all coagulation factors compared to adults

answer:
The correct answer is E.

Neonates have lower levels of most coagulation factors, but not all of them. FVIII is typically found in greater levels in neonates than in adults. FVIII is not made in the liver. Most other coagulation factors are made in the liver, and in neonates their levels are lower due to the liver being immature.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: Which of the following is FALSE regarding von Willebrand disease (vWD)?

Women with vWD should avoid using oral contraceptives
Those with type O blood typically have less vWF than non-O type blood

answer:
The correct answer is D.

The oral contraceptive pill has procoagulant properties can help women with vWB manage heavy menstrual bleeding. vWD the most common inherited bleeding disorder and is tested for by investigating vWF antigen, vWF activity, FVIII level, and blood group. DDVAP can be used to help managed vWD. Those with type O blood typically have ~30% less vWF than those with other blood types.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: Which of the following is NOT a step in your general approach to thrombocytopenia?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

The 1st step when approaching thrombocytopenia should be to confirm that thrombocytopenia is present. This can be done with a CBC. Step 2 is to assess the severity. This is done clinically by identifying whether or not bleeding is present, the site of bleeding, and how severe the bleeding is. The platelet count on the CBC will also provide an idea of how severe the thrombocytopenia is. The 3rd step is to consider the differential diagnosis. There are a variety of causes of thrombocytopenia that fall under the categories of decreased production, increased destruction, or sequestration of platelets, or others (pseudothrombocytopenia). Step 4 is to consider associated disorders. The 5th and final step is to put findings together to create a management plan (not an option in question). Assessing the bone marrow is not a mandatory step in assessing thrombocytopenia, although it could be done in rare cases where the majority of causes of thrombocytopenia have been ruled out and there is no identifiable explanation of the thrombocytopenia.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.
stem: Which of the following is NOT a cause of decreased thrombocyte production?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

von Willebrand disease is a disease that affects secondary hemostasis and does not result in reduced platelet production. The liver produces thrombopoietin which stimulates thrombocyte production, and liver disease can affect thrombopoietin production. Vitamin B12 is required for DNA synthesis; vitamin B12 deficiency can result in thrombocytopenia, among other conditions. Aplastic anemia is a condition of bone marrow failure and results in pancytopenia, which includes thrombocyte production. Myelofibrosis is a similar condition where the bone marrow is replaced with fibrous tissue and can result in thrombocytopenia.

lectureMeta: Written fresh by the Meds 2025 volunteers (December 2021). The bank states on its own second page that these were not verified by faculty.

Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) is characterized by acute kidney injury, the presence of spherocytes, and acute thrombocytopenia

Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) is characterized by acute kidney injury and acute thrombocytopenia, but not the presence of spherocytes. Instead, schistocytes are seen.

stem: Which of the following is most commonly used to investigate possible iron deficiency?
answer:
The correct answer is B.

Although ferritin mainly stores iron within cells, a small amount leaks into the circulation and is valuable clinically as a measure of how much iron is stored in the body. A, C and E are currently used only for diagnosis of iron overload, not iron deficiency. Prussian blue staining of bone marrow aspirate and/or biopsy is the gold standard for measuring iron stores, but is not used as commonly as serum ferritin.

stem: Body homeostasis of iron is controlled by:
answer:
The correct answer is C.

Intestinal cells are sensitive to the total amount of iron stored in the body; high stores decrease absorption and low stores increase absorption. Cells in the crypt of the intestine are underdeveloped and mature as they move up the villus. Exposure to iron in the undeveloped state is critical to the levels of iron transporters once they reach the villus. When iron levels are high at the level of the crypt cell, transporters will be down-regulated to decrease intestinal absorption and vice versa.

answer:
The correct answer is D.

The correct answer is B.

Supplement both folate and cobalamin in order to prevent possible neurologic complications
Adjust the folate supplementation to 10mg/day for pregnant women, especially those in the first trimester who are at highest risk of birth defects from folate deficiency

answer:
The correct answer is B.

A Direct Antiglobulin Test that comes back positive for anti-Rhesus antibody
The presence of spherocytes on the patient’s blood film

stem: Which of the following is part of the diagnostic criteria for polycythemia vera (PV):
answer:
The correct answer is B.

A. No – PRV involves erythrocytosis, which will increase rather than decrease patients’ hemoglobin. Hb > 185 in men or >165 in women is one of the WHO 2008 major criteria for diagnosis. B. Yes – Erythrocytes are being produced in excess of the body’s requirements, and the body responds by shutting down erythropoietin production, which would decrease erythrocyte production if the cells had not escaped from normal regulatory control. Low erythropoietin is one of the minor criteria (WHO 2008) for diagnosis of PRV. C. No – A JAK2 V617F or JAK2 exon 12 mutation is one of the major criteria for diagnosis of PRV, and about 90% of PRV cases have one of these mutations identified. They allow activation of JAK- STAT pathways without the ligand-binding normally required, effectively disrupting normal regulation. D. No – Sickle Cell anemia is not related. E. No – although post-bath pruritis is a common and characteristic symptom of PRV, it is not one of the diagnostic criteria.

stem: Oncogenesis can arise due to mutations within the genome. Two known mechanisms of oncogenesis involve mutations to proto-oncogenes and tumour suppressor genes. These two mechanisms of oncogenesis differ from one another in that:

options.html: Proto-oncogene mutations result in malignant transformation while tumour suppressor gene mutations tend to produce benign neoplasms
Tumour suppressor gene mutations tend to be point mutations while proto-oncogenes tend to be from frameshift mutations
Proto-oncogene mutations result in loss of regulation within the cell cycle while tumour suppressor mutations do not
Tumour suppressor genes require mutations to both homologous alleles (two-hit hypothesis) to result in oncogenesis while proto-oncogenes require only one allelic mutation

answer:
The correct answer is D.

A. False. Both proto-oncogene and tumour suppressor gene mutations can produce malignant transformation of cells. An example of a malignancy that is a result of a mutation to a proto-oncogene is CML which results from the BRC-ABL translocation between chromosomes 9 & 22. Mutations to the p53 tumour suppressor gene can produce cancers of the breast, brain, adrenal glands and sarcomas. B. False. Point mutations, DNA amplification, & chromosomal rearrangement are all common mechanisms of mutation in oncogene activation. The two major types of mutations involved in tumour suppressor gene mutations are point mutations and large deletions. C. False. Both types of mutations result in the loss of oversight in the cell cycle which permits unrestrained cell proliferation. D. Correct. Proto-oncogenes generally only require a mutation in one allele to become oncogenes and acts in a dominant fashion. Tumour suppressor genes generally require mutations to both homologous alleles before suppressor activity is completely lost. This is attributable to the diploid nature of human cells which permits suppressor activity in the unaffected allele should the homologous allele suffers a mutation.

His low platelet count is likely the result of a hereditary condition

answer:
The correct answer is A.

This patient has a low platelet count. The causes of thrombocytopenia may be broken down broadly into: increased destruction, decreased production, and increased sequestration. In this case, the most likely cause is bone marrow suppression by MTX causing decreased production. There are no causes of destruction of platelets or hypersplenism in this case.

The correct answer is B.

stem: A 3-year-old patient had a cough and runny nose for 4 days. He now presents to your clinic one week after his symptoms subsided with his father, who says that his child has developed “red rashes” on his legs that have been bleeding easily, for the last 2 days. CBC shows his platelet count to be 21 x 109/L (low), with a normal Hb. What is the best course of management for this patient?

options.html: No treatment, follow to spontaneous remission

answer:
The correct answer is C.

This is a case of acute Immune Thrombocytopenia Purpura in a child. This is supported by the isolated low platelet count, and the preceding viral infection. Symptomatic acute ITP requires treatment, and IVIG should be used in children to spare steroid use (i.e. no prednisone). Platelet transfusion and splenectomy may be beneficial in cases of chronic ITP, but would not be appropriate in this setting.

stem: A patient whom you have diagnosed with hemophilia type A presents to your clinic. Which of the following laboratory abnormalities would be expected in this patient?

options.html: Prolonged INR due to impedance of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation
Prolonged INR due to impedance of the intrinsic pathway of coagulation
Prolonged aPTT due to impedance of the extrinsic pathway of coagulation
Prolonged aPTT due to impedance of the intrinsic pathway of coagulation
Prolonged INR and aPTT due to impedance of both the intrinsic and extrinsic pathway of coagulation

answer:
The correct answer is D.

aPTT relates to the intrinsic pathway, while INR (akaProthrombin Time) relates to the extrinsic pathway. In Hemophilia A the Factor VIII gene is affected, resulting in an impedance of the intrinsic pathway, while leaving other Factors (including those of the extrinsic pathway) intact. Note that Hemophilia B (Factor IX affected) would also result in an increased aPTT.

answer:

What is the most likely diagnosis in this patient?
answer:
The correct answer is C.

For a patient with ecchymosis (as described here) one should perform a work-up of secondary hemostasis problems. Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis:
answer:
The correct answer is B.

The increased aPTT and normal INR suggest a problem with the intrinsic pathway alone (eliminating d) and e) which would alter the INR). stem: A 56-year-old man is referred to you for consult after his lab results indicated normal blood counts, a normal INR and an aPTT value that was triple the maximum accepted normal value. He had undergone surgery a few days earlier and was recovering in the hospital. He has not had any bleeding episodes from any of his IV lines or arterial lines, and has no visible petechiae or ecchymoses. He has no history of hemophilia and is not taking any anticoagulant or antiplatelet medications. What is the most likely explanation of his abnormal lab findings?
answer:
The correct answer is D.

The high aPTT suggests an abnormality with the intrinsic pathway, which makes b) and c) unlikely. DIC is unlikely because the patient is well, and the platelet count and INR are unaffected here. The most likely scenario is that the sample was drawn through an access line containing heparin, which is known to affect the intrinsic pathway. Re-drawing the sample with a tube that does not contain heparin would likely show a normal aPTT value.
